item.title: Church not a political party — Bishop Mike Okonkwo
item.description: By Olayinka Latona The Fountain of Life Church today held its Sunday service despite reports of a court injunction against Pastor Jimmy Odukoya. Addressing the crowded congregation, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya said he had not received any court injunction as reported, and stressed his unwavering love for the church. Members were said to have chanted “We love you” during the service. Bishop Mike Okonkwo of The Redeemed Evangelical Ministry, one of the spiritual fathers to the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, ministered on the theme “The Glory of The Church.” He charged members and ministers of the church to diligently keep the founder’s legacy and remain steadfast in Christ, reminding them of the advice he gave when the church founder died. “The responsibility fell on us to talk to… The only honour we can do for the sacrifice, the process, pains and everything that the man of God who is highly celebrated in this country is that his legacy must continue,” Bishop Okonkwo said. “And I told you that day that Fountain will never die. No matter the trial or temptation, this is a work that is solidly laid. The price has been paid; lives have been lost. There is no power of hell that would destroy this work. It will go from glory to glory.” Acknowledging recent online attacks, he said: “For the past one or two weeks, we have been literally battered on social media. There is nothing that has not been said, both what is true and what is not true. Phone calls from far and near: ‘Bishop Mike, where are you?’ You can’t separate me from Fountain; it’s not possible, because it’s a covenant established by God Himself. What affects Fountain affects me. Don’t think that I am just aloof. I said to myself, ‘God, you just have to give us wisdom.’” He added: “The day you fully understand the glory of God upon His church and what it takes to give birth to His church, then there is nothing from the gates of hell that will move you.” Bishop Okonkwo warned that the church is not a political party but God’s house. “The church is not a human institution; it’s God’s house; it belongs to Him. Think of the price that He paid for the church. We should all know that we are not for Tolu, Jimmy or the Board of Trustees; none of them died for you,” he said. “The church is not a political party because Jesus Christ’s life was involved. The church is not an ordinary thing. We must be careful that none of us is an instrument to destroy the church of Christ.” He declared that God is interested in the church and that its best days are ahead. “God is interested in this church, in case you don’t know. What you have seen so far cannot be compared to what is coming, because everything that has to do with God is always progressive. This church is going to do seven more than what Pastor Taiwo left it,” he said. “We must appreciate the predetermined plans of God concerning each and every one of us. You’re a vital, relevant, valued part of God’s global agenda for the human race worldwide… God values

item.title: 49ers-Vikings roundtable: Mexico City showdown between two of NFC's best
item.description: Quarterback Brock Purdy and the 49ers offense have faced four defenses in the bottom six of the NFL this season - the Falcons, Cowboys, Cardinals and Raiders - possibly skewing their effectiveness. (Tony Gutierrez/Associated Press) The San Francisco 49ers have already delivered some big wins - the opener in Australia against the Rams and beating the Seahawks in Seattle among them - but suddenly their game in Mexico City against a really good Minnesota Vikings team might be their biggest test yet. Before the two teams tangle, we asked columnist Ann Killion and reporters Eric Branch and Harrison Rich for their answers to some key questions about the matchup. Have mounting injuries already ended the prime of Nick Bosa 's career? Is this his new normal in terms of production? Harrison Rich: Bosa has not looked like his old self since returning two weeks ago from a calf injury. He didn't look like himself earlier in the season, either, when he was dealing with knee tendinitis coming off his second torn right ACL. The 29-year-old defensive end hasn't recorded a sack in four games this season, his longest NFL drought. He pointed to two factors Wednesday for his struggles: He's still learning some of the quirks of defensive coordinator Raheem Morris' scheme, and he's still knocking off some rust. Bosa said he took "for granted" some of the things he used to be able to do automatically. Sunday's game, expected to have playoff-like intensity, will tell us a lot about the heights Bosa is still capable of reaching. Ann Killion: It's probably safe to say that Bosa will never again be the dominant force that he was in 2021 and 2022. Four years later, he's 29 and has a history of serious knee injuries. The fact that he thought, as he said this week, that he could "coast" and do the things he used to do "automatically" is an indication of just how hard it is for elite athletes to stay at that level, not only physically but mentally. Bosa's honest assessment this week means he will be even more in the spotlight in Sunday's game, where Minnesota's pass rush is expected to be the star. Eric Branch: It's a question Bosa might be asking himself. It was notable this week that Bosa admitted he was surprised he hasn't been able to return from last year's torn ACL and "automatically" perform at his All-Pro level. His extensive medical file includes three torn ACLs, two on the right knee he injured in 2025. Still, Bosa has shown some dominant flashes, such as when he hit Dak Prescott's arm in mid-throw last Sunday in Dallas after bullying right tackle Terence Steele with a bull rush. Also, Bosa has played in just four games this season, which qualifies as a small sample size. Verdict: It's premature to bury Bosa. Who has the edge when quarterback Kirk Cousins faces the 49ers defense for the second time in three weeks after he was traded from the Raiders to the Vikings? item.title: Randy Flores brings a former player's perspective to Houston Astros GM job - and knows its limits
item.description: From player to scout to Astros GM, Randy Flores says firsthand experience helps him understand players - if he stays open to other perspectives. (Jason Fochtman/Houston Chronicle) In his first year as St. Louis Cardinals scouting director , Randy Flores was watching a pitcher who threw a four-seam fastball and a curveball. The mix can be the backbone of a north-south pitching profile. But to Flores, a former major-league reliever, it looked suboptimal. "I'm like, ‘No, no, no - you sink it and slide it,'" said Flores, reciting an approach he gleaned from former Cardinals pitching coach Dave Duncan. As a slight left-hander who did not throw especially hard, Flores carved out a playing career that lasted parts of eight major-league seasons. So, his methods had merit. But as an executive now, he recalls the scouting anecdote as something of a cautionary tale. "Being a former player, if you're anchored too much to, ‘This is how it was done when I was playing,' it's the wrong thing," Flores said. Exploring other perspectives and means and finding a balance has been part of Flores' evolution as an executive, one that led to his hiring this month as general manager of the Houston Astros . It is also an arc to which only a handful of the majors' current highest-ranking baseball executives can relate. Of the current presidents of baseball operations, Jerry Dipoto (Mariners), Chris Young (Rangers), Craig Breslow (Red Sox) and Buster Posey (Giants) played in the majors. So did general managers Chris Getz (White Sox) and Flores, whom the Astros hired after 11-plus seasons in St. Louis' front office. That many top executives did not play in the majors, or at all professionally, illustrates how it is far from required. It might even invite the question of how such experience informs former players' approach to the role, if at all, as Flores settles into running a baseball operations department for the first time. "You probably have more empathy … for what a player goes through, from the moment they sign their first professional contract to when they get to the big leagues," Dipoto said at last week's GM meetings in Las Vegas. Dipoto and Breslow were relievers in the majors, like Flores. Dipoto posited that background could help "to understand the life of the guy who (is) not always the most thought-of player on the roster." "Outside of that, I think it's just business as usual," Dipoto said. "We each went through our own, I guess, apprenticeship (after playing). "You take the lessons you learn and apply them, just like any other general manager does when they get their first job. We just maybe have that slight - I don't even want to call it an advantage - that slight difference in that we have lived life in these players' shoes and probably as a result have a little bit more empathy rather than just frustration. It's a hard game." Mariners GM Jerry Dipoto, a former major league reliever, is among a half-dozen ex-players who head up baseball operations departmen

item.title: Liverpool remain unsure over Virgil van Dijk contract decision
item.description: Liverpool remain unsure over Virgil van Dijk contract decision Virgil van Dijk contract latest as Liverpool weigh renewal and AC Milan interest Liverpool are facing a significant call on the future of Virgil van Dijk, with fresh reporting from Sport Italia indicating that the club remain hesitant over the defender’s preferred contract terms. Van Dijk, now 35, remains one of the defining figures of this Liverpool side. Even through major change, including the end of the Arne Slot era and the arrival of Andoni Iraola, his place in the team has carried real weight. His level, leadership and authority have kept him central to Liverpool’s defensive structure, while younger players around him continue to develop. The issue is not whether Van Dijk still contributes. By all accounts, he does. The issue is what Liverpool are prepared to commit to next, and on what financial and sporting terms. Sport Italia report outlines key Virgil van Dijk dilemma The update from Italy points to a familiar modern stand-off between club caution and player expectation. Sport Italia state, “Gerry Cardinale is following the Reds captain’s situation and dreams of a big signing this summer. The sticking point is a renewal: the Dutchman is asking for a two-year contract, while Liverpool still seem unconvinced.” That immediately places AC Milan into the conversation, albeit at a watching distance for now. The same report adds, “Virgil van Dijk’s future could become one of the most interesting situations of the upcoming summer transfer window. AC Milan is in the background, with Gerry Cardinale eyeing the possibility of bringing one of the most authoritative defenders in the international scene to San Siro.” There is still an important caveat. Liverpool hold the contract, and the club’s decision remains the key factor. As Sport Italia put it, “But before imagining the Dutch centre-back in a Rossoneri shirt, Liverpool must be taken into account.” That is where the matter sharpens. “This is precisely where the crux of the matter lies: Van Dijk wants a two-year extension, while Liverpool do not appear willing, at least for now, to fully grant his request.” Photo: IMAGO Liverpool contract policy under focus again This feels less about emotion and more about policy. Van Dijk is Liverpool’s highest-paid player, and by the start of next season he will be 36. Clubs at the elite end have to judge not only present performance, but the durability of that performance over the life of a deal. Even so, there is a strong football case for meeting him somewhere close to his request. Liverpool are still in a period of squad adjustment. Defensive planning matters, and certainty matters more. Van Dijk’s ongoing importance, on the pitch and inside the dressing room, means a short-term approach carries risk if there is no fully trusted successor ready to step in immediately. item.title: How to watch Liverpool vs Man United: TV guide and streaming options
item.description: How to watch Liverpool vs Man United: TV guide and streaming options Liverpool vs Manchester United Preview as Mauricio Pochettino Begins with Anfield Trip Few managerial openings come with a harsher introduction than an away day at Anfield, yet that is exactly what awaits Mauricio Pochettino in his first match as Manchester United head coach. The Argentine has arrived in the north-west after the international break and, within days of taking charge, is already staring down one of the Premier League’s biggest fixtures. It is a huge moment for Manchester United, who have made a dreadful start to the season and sit in the relegation zone. With only one league win to their name so far, that success coming against Ipswich Town on matchday two, the scale of the task in front of Pochettino is impossible to ignore. Anfield has often exposed uncertainty and fragility, and United need a response immediately. Liverpool Form Under Andoni Iraola Liverpool head into this contest in far stronger shape. Under Andoni Iraola, the side have found rhythm, intensity and belief, giving the impression of a team settling quickly into a clear identity. That momentum makes them favourites for this meeting, particularly with home support expecting a statement performance in one of English football’s defining rivalries. There is, however, an interesting recent wrinkle in this fixture. Liverpool are winless at home against Manchester United in their last three meetings. Their last Anfield victory over their old rivals remains the unforgettable 7-0 demolition in 2023, a result that still looms large whenever these clubs meet on Merseyside. Photo IMAGO Mauricio Pochettino and Manchester United Pressure Pochettino will hope to use that recent record at Anfield as a small source of encouragement. More than anything, he needs to bring structure, calm and resilience to a side that has looked short on confidence. A point would steady the mood, while a spirited display could offer the first signs that Manchester United are ready to climb out of trouble. Premier League Stakes at Anfield For Liverpool, this is a chance to keep pace at the top end of the Premier League and reassert authority at home. For Manchester United, it is about survival, belief and a new manager trying to shift the tone in record time. That contrast makes this latest Liverpool vs Manchester United clash especially compelling. The spotlight will naturally fall on Pochettino, but Liverpool will see only opportunity. If Iraola’s side maintain their current level, Anfield could prove every bit as daunting as it looks for a manager with barely enough time to unpack before facing the fire. item.title: ABUAD warns students against cultism, cybercrime
item.description: Varsity matriculates 2,442 students for 2026/2027 session By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI — Afe Babalola University, Ado-Ekiti (ABUAD), has warned newly admitted students against cultism, cybercrime, substance abuse and other social vices capable of undermining their education and future. The university also cautioned the students against examination malpractice, bullying and the irresponsible use of artificial intelligence, urging them to uphold discipline, integrity and academic excellence. The Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Smaranda Olarinde, gave the warning at the institution’s 18th matriculation ceremony held over the weekend, where 2,442 students were formally admitted for the 2026/2027 academic session. The figure comprises 2,089 regular undergraduate students, 77 Open and Distance Learning students and 276 part-time students. Giving a breakdown of the undergraduate admissions, Olarinde said 306 students were admitted into the College of Social and Management Sciences, 307 into Sciences, 275 into Pharmacy, 684 into Medicine and Health Sciences, 171 into Law and 346 into Engineering. Addressing the students, the vice-chancellor described their admission as an opportunity that required discipline, responsibility and commitment to academic excellence. She urged them to be mindful of their associations, noting that their choice of friends could influence their habits, reputation, academic performance and future. According to her, university education goes beyond obtaining certificates to include character formation, emotional maturity, leadership development and the acquisition of values needed to contribute meaningfully to society. Olarinde urged the students to uphold the university’s philosophy of Labour, Service and Integrity, stressing that hard work, selfless service and honesty should guide their academic and professional pursuits. She also cautioned against the misuse of artificial intelligence and other emerging digital technologies, warning students not to present machine-generated materials or another person’s intellectual work as their original research. “The company you keep will influence your habits, attitude, reputation and ultimately your destiny. Surround yourselves with people who encourage learning, discipline, honesty and constructive ambition. “Stay away from cultism, substance abuse, bullying, examination malpractice, cybercrime and every other form of misconduct that can destroy your future and bring disrepute to your family and this university. “No momentary pleasure or misguided friendship is worth the sacrifice of your education, character or good name,” she said. On the use of artificial intelligence, the vice-chancellor said the technology could support research, improve productivity and create new opportunities for learning, but should not replace independent thinking, genuine scholarship or personal integrity. “Use digital tools responsibly. item.title: Miami Heat NBA Game Draws 95% New Shoppers For GTA VI Launch
item.description: Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Miami Heat turned a regular basketball game into a global video game launch. On Wednesday night, the Kaseya Center became the setting for the world premiere of Grand Theft Auto VI. This event blended the sport with gaming culture in a way few teams have ever tried. The arena makeover attracted a huge wave of fans who had never bought a ticket before. Hardwood floors and food stands transformed into spots from the new game. Lines for fictional eateries such as Burger Shot and Cluckin’ Bell were passed by walking fans. The attempt to make the entire structure resemble the game yielded immediate results. Local reporter Will Manso shared footage of packed concourse crowds, admitting he had never seen lines that long. According to Yahoo Sports , 95 percent of shoppers inside the team store were new. A Fresh Look for the Court The visual changes went deep into the design of the playing surface. During their 137-130 win over the Milwaukee Bucks, Miami players sported special Vice City-themed jerseys. To align with the game’s style, the court displayed vibrant pink, blue, and black colors. The center court featured “Vice City” while the iconic “VI” logo was integrated into the design. This unique setup helped celebrate the long-awaited release of the sixth installment in the series. Merchandise sales exploded as fans rushed to own a piece of the night. Yahoo Sports reports that the black Court Culture “Vice City” Hoodie comes in adult sizes. Some items sold out fast, but five Vice-themed hats remain in stock online. On-Court Wins and Off-Court Talk The game theme drew the crowds, but the on-court action delivered a dominant win for the Heat. In his debut against his former team, Giannis Antetokounmpo tallied 27 points. He also secured 14 rebounds and distributed 9 assists. Hot Hot Hoops reports that Miami outscored Milwaukee by 12 points in his minutes, as he missed a triple-double by a single assist. Davion Mitchell scored 24 on efficient shooting while Bam Adebayo contributed 26 points. While the team celebrated, some media figures criticized the players for their excitement. ESPN analyst Stephen A. Smith did not restrain his criticism of multiple NBA stars regarding their enthusiasm for the highly anticipated GTA VI. On The Stephen A. Bam Adebayo and Klay Thompson, stars of the Miami Heat, were criticized by Smith, for discussing their plan to go home and play the long-awaited GTA VI. Building a Legacy Through Class Despite the noise from critics, the event highlighted smart business for the franchise. Fans viewed the tribute videos as smart business that is a recruitment tool. They tell future prospects that regardless of tenure or outcome, dignity remains assured when the partnership concludes. Wednesday night was about more than just Tyler Herro and Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kel’el Ware or Kasparas Jakucionis. item.title: England won't get carried away by All Blacks win
item.description: [BBC] In his latest BBC Sport column, England World Cup winner Matt Dawson reflects on Steve Borthwick's side's record win over New Zealand and previews the final round of Nations Championship fixtures. If England had produced that performance two years ago against New Zealand, there would have been a lap of honour and wild celebrations. Saturday felt like business. Job done, move on. And that is how it should be. It was a record victory for a northern hemisphere side against the All Blacks, yet at full-time you would hardly have known it. Even the post-match messaging from their leaders - Maro Itoje, Ellis Genge and Steve Borthwick - was that this performance had always been in them and that nobody was surprised. However, they will want to back it up. A tired but hurting New Zealand side will arrive at Allianz Stadium next Saturday looking for revenge. England beat the All Blacks in back-to-back Tests in 2002 and 2003. Matching that achievement on Saturday was a significant statement. Three consecutive wins over New Zealand, followed by a third-place finish, would leave England in a strong position heading into 2027, when the Rugby World Cup takes place in Australia. Lose, though, and it will be a waste of some great momentum. We have had many a false dawn with Borthwick's England, but something feels different this time. For me, that comes down to the players taking responsibility. Many of us ex-pros called for it during the Six Nations, and finally we are seeing the players take the lead on the style of rugby they want to play. It is an exciting, free-flowing brand of attacking rugby that mirrors what they are used to playing in the Prem. England's backs can compete with the very best and they tore through New Zealand on multiple occasions. Credit also has to go to Borthwick for allowing the players to take control. That, in itself, shows how he is learning and evolving as a head coach. Once players start getting 40, 50, 60 or 70 caps, they know more about certain aspects of the game than the coach because they are the ones out there experiencing it. If the environment does not allow players to turn around and say 'this isn't going to work', then it is never going to work. The reports before the Australia game suggested honest conversations took place, with the players wanting a greater say in how the team operates. The Six Nations was probably a big turning point. The change in mood and the feel-good factor are clear in the way England are carrying themselves. They now feel in control and, crucially, have a genuine sense of ownership in shaping the team and how it plays. 'An enormous statement about English rugby' Lewis Moody, a former team-mate of mine, joining the team to face the New Zealand haka was an enormous statement about English rugby. Whether you are playing in 2026 or 1926, this is England rugby. We are together. It was a united and extraordinary moment, one that will stay with me until the day I die. item.title: Chelsea boss Bompastor calls for better balance after draw at Liverpool
item.description: Chelsea boss Bompastor calls for better balance after draw at Liverpool Chelsea head coach Sonia Bompastor said that her her side need more balance between attack and defence after they drew 0-0 at Liverpool on Saturday afternoon. The Blues had chances to win the game, but they were unable to take full advantage as they dropped points in the title race. Speaking to the media after the match, Bompastor said that her side must have greater balance between defence and attack. “I’m really happy with a lot of things we are doing right now,” Bompastor said. “When you have ambitions, when you want to win titles, you need to make sure to find the right balance between being strong defensively, but also, being able to score goals. “I would like to have a better balance in terms of being able to score more.” Bompastor left it late to make attacking changes. Aggie Beever-Jones was not introduced until the 83rd minute. The Blues boss defended her decisions in the game. She said “I think all my decisions are based on performances. I think even if we were not able to score a goal in this game, what I was seeing on the pitch was good enough for me to still be confident. I think at this level, when you bring players even for 10, 12, 15 minutes, it’s enough for them to show and to prove, it didn’t happen today. I think the team [that] started was probably the team who was performing the best in training, games and everything.” Lola Brown made only her second WSL start and made a positive impact. Bompastor was full of praise for the youngster. She said “Lola hasn’t got many minutes because the competition is high in this squad, we have a lot of experienced players. I think what she’s been doing since this summer has been good, really good. “Her mentality is unbelievable. She always works hard and she puts a bigger foot on the pitch. I think the quality she brings with the ball, she’s a really confident player. “I just felt from what I could observe in this game, she was probably the right profile to come on in the game as a left wing-back. I think we wanted to create more with crosses. “I think she did well. We couldn’t convert some of the crosses she put in the box. I think from everyone I had available on the bench, she was probably the right profile to come on.” Chelsea have three games following the international break and Bompastor is already sharing the importance of what it means. She said “I think next block is three games, so it will be quick, they are already important. I think for us, we’ll keep continuing to work, that’s always what we have been doing. Right now, we need to find a better balance between the defensive aspects and with the way we build-up, no matter of the opponents; if they come and man-mark, if they leave us a little bit more space. We also need to improve creation, finishing phase, making sure we create as much as possible in the games and we are just clinical in the box when we have those opportunities.” Chelsea return to action afte

item.title: ‘Embrace the love, America!’ – Young couple appear to break-up and make-up during Georgia Tech game
item.description: Photo by Eldon Lindsay/Georgia Tech Athletics/University Images via Getty Images Broadcast cameras caught a young couple at the Georgia Tech game having an argument, before later finding them having reconciled. College football games usually feature young fans in attendance trying increasingly bizarre tactics to try and get the attention of the TV cameras. However, one young couple at the Georgia Tech game would have hoped that their private interaction wouldn’t be broadcast on national television. Random college couple’s spat and reconciliation caught on ESPN cameras During Georgia Tech’s game against Wake Forest, ESPN cameras found a young couple sitting in the stands seemingly in the middle of an argument. While the broadcasters were speculating about the exchange, they did suggest that the pair were having an intense conversation, even using graphics to illustrate the nature of their conversation. Later in the game, the cameras panned back to the young couple, only to find them sharing an embrace having seemingly reconciled after the argument. “This is great! Embrace the love, America,” remarked the commentators when they were shown on the television feed. While the result on the field was not going Georgia Tech’s way, given that they were blown out 29-50 by Wake Forest, the young couple will be glad to have walked away from the game with their relationship intact. Unfortunately for them, their relationship became the subject of intense speculation on a national basis because of ESPN’s decision to aim their cameras on them while they were in the middle of a private conversation. Hopefully, they take the incident in their strides and don’t let the outside noise affect them and their relationship too much. item.title: UH helmet stickers: Cougars' top performers in Week 12 win at West Virginia
item.description: Houston Cougars wide receiver Amare Thomas (0) runs to the endzone for a touchdown after a catch against West Virginia Mountaineers during the first half of an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026, in Morgantown, W.Va. (AP Photo/William Wotring) (William Wotring/Associated Press) MORGANTOWN, W.Va. - Top performers in No. 20 Houston's 34-31 victory over West Virginia : Keisean Henderson What a debut for the Cougars' quarterback of the future. Pressed into an emergency start with fifth-year senior Conner Weigman injured , Henderson directed two scoring drives in the final 5 ½ minutes as the Cougars rallied from a 10-point deficit to win on the road. The heralded freshman threw a touchdown on his first pass. He finished 18 of 28 for 268 yards against the Power Four's worst defense. "I wanted my teammates to know, and I was telling them on the sideline and letting them know that just because I'm a freshman, that doesn't mean I don't have a mindset to go out and win," Henderson said. Jonathan Dimas Dimas added another chapter to his clutch season, sealing the win with a 23-yard field goal as time expired. He also connected from 34 yards as he improved to 13-of-15 on field-goal attempts this season. His 54-yard attempt - which would have been a school record - hit the left upright. Sign up for Cougar Confidential You'll get get in-depth news and analysis about UH's basketball and football teams from reporter Joseph Duarte by signing up for the Cougar Confidential newsletter . Makhi Hughes Hughes had the best rushing performance by a UH running back in nearly a decade, finishing with 158 yards and three touchdowns. It was the most rushing yards by a UH back since Duke Catalon had 177 against SMU in 2017 . Hughes scored on runs of 21, 2 and 3 yards, with the last tying the score late in the fourth quarter. He nearly had a fourth touchdown on a 71-yard run before being pulled down just short of the end zone. Jaden Yates Welcome back, Jaden. Yates, who has worked his way into a productive role after missing a month due to injury, recorded a career-high 16 tackles. One of his biggest came when he stopped 1,000-yard rusher Cam Cook on West Virginia's final drive, helping force a punt. His tackle total was the most by a Cougar since Austin Robinson had 21 against Navy in 2018 . Trent Walker Walker earns a sticker for his critical 22-yard punt return that helped set up the game-winning field goal. Will James West Virginia didn't throw often, but when it did, the veteran cornerback was usually nearby. He finished with a career-high four pass breakups. item.title: No. 5 Texas hosts Southern Indiana with plenty to improve upon
item.description: Dec 16, 2025; Austin, Texas, USA; Texas Longhorns head coach Sean Miller takes a time out during the second half against the Le Moyne Dolphins at Moody Center. Mandatory Credit: Dustin Safranek-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Before heading to the Rady Children’s Invitational in San Diego for two games over the Thanksgiving break, the No. 6 Texas Longhorns remain at the Moody Center, hosting the Southern Indiana Screaming Eagles on Sunday at 2 p.m. Central on SEC Network+. There are plenty of coaching points for Texas to implement after Thursday’s disappointing 92-68 victory over Southern Utah that required the Longhorns to go on a late run to finally create separation after almost 30 minutes of disappointing basketball. Playing at a deliberate pace that put increased pressure on Texas to avoid late-clock fouls, defensive breakdowns, and giving up offensive rebounds, Southern Utah operated with a high level of efficiency in the first half and well into the second half, shooting 50 percent overall and 50 percent from three heading into halftime down just three points after leading by as many as nine points in the first half. “We had a hard time guarding them. I think we’ve taken a lot of pride in being a better defensive team. I thought, to a large extent on Sunday against Baylor, we really showed that we were able to get key stops, and we had a lot of athleticism — if you watch that game closely, we flew around and covered for each other,” Miller said in his post-game press conference. “Tonight, we just were in mud. We just we weren’t able to do that, and I think some of it was their style, some of it is our readiness.” On Friday and Saturday, a primary point of emphasis for head coach Sean Miller was closing out better against shooters after Baylor went 11-of-25 shooting from three (44 percent) and Southern Utah found similar success on 10-of-23 shooting beyond the arc (43.5 percent). In drive-and kick situations over the first three games, the Horns only allowed 0.7 points per possession, but the last two contests saw Texas give up 1.29 points per possession, a disappointing number that came as a result of simple dribble penetration and slow rotations playing hedge coverage against the pick and roll. An area where Texas' perimeter defense is being challenged: attack-and-kick situations First three games: 0.70 PPP allowed Against Baylor & Southern Utah: 1.29 PPP allowed The numbers point to an area the Longhorns need to clean up. #HookEm | #Texas pic.twitter.com/7bKEGsXGOi — Jalen Brown (@jalenpolobrown) November 21, 2026 In discussing his team’s closeouts against the Thunderbirds, Miller voiced his frustrations in a manner only slightly more mild than his most irritated moments last season. “It’s like you kind of come at a shooter on a closeout, right, the ball is traveling to your shooter, you’re closing out on him, and it’s like you got some cookies, you got some milk. item.title: Porto rally around defender that was left in tears by horror own goal
item.description: Porto have rallied around Francisco Moura after the player scored a horror own goal in his side’s Portuguese Cup tie on Friday, which reduced him to tears. The 27-year-old defender passed the ball into his own net in the 57th minute of the fourth-round tie against third-division side Paredes, inexplicably kicking it into the bottom left corner after a save by his goalkeeper. Moura dropped straight to the ground with his hands over his face, covering his head with his jersey as he started crying. He then signalled to the bench that he wanted to be substituted. Moura, who received support from both sets of players following the blunder, was not immediately substituted and later came off in the 70th minute. Empata o USC Paredes numa infelicidade de Francisco Moura 🫨 #sporttvportugal #TAÇAnaSPORTTV #TaçadePortugal #FCPorto #USCParedes pic.twitter.com/KqQQkxEPDq — sport tv (@sporttvportugal) November 20, 2026 The episode prompted a call for support for Moura during Porto's general assembly on Saturday, which drew applause from fellow members. “Members took the opportunity to express their vote of confidence in Francisco Moura,” Porto's general assembly chairman Antonio Tavares said. "Even though things sometimes go wrong, the members made it clear today that they fully understand the situation and stand in solidarity with him, sending him a warm embrace and wishing him success.” Club president Andre Villas-Boas also endorsed the call for support. The cup tie finished 1-1 after extra time, with Porto eventually overcoming Paredes on penalties. Moura had previously faced abuse on social media. He restricted comments on Instagram after conceding a late handball penalty that led to Sporting Lisbon’s equaliser in a league game in February, then temporarily deactivated his account following a draw at Benfica in March.

item.title: Wrestling Travels to The C.J. Morgan Invitational
item.description: Penn State Wrestling makes their annual trip up the Hudson Valley to West Point for the erstwhile Black Knight Invitational. It’s the same tournament but a new name dedicated to former Army West Point wrestler C.J. Morgan who lost his life in a military vehicle accident. Links Audio with Ironhead starts at 9:40 am: “Lionvision” Free Brackets and Subscription Streaming: Flowrestling Others squads at the tournament include Army West Point, Bloomsburg, Columbia, Hofstra and VMI. Not the stiffest of competition but it’s a great opportunity to blow your lungs out as the wrestlers work on early season conditioning. And, probably more importantly, this event serves as unofficial wrestle offs as the coaches look to set the line up for the season. This year most of the lineup is set with one exception, the matchup to watch is Masanosuke Ono and Nate Desmond at 133 pounds. Coach Cael indicated that Ono won the wrestle off in the practice room but Desmond continues to push and this event should serve as one more data point to determing the starter. Ono continues to work on his folk style chops while Desmond, you may recall, wants to win this event again as he handed Lilledahl his only, albeit unofficial, loss of the 2026 season a year ago. We also get our first look at Freshman heavyweight Elijah Wood. He’s reported to be working on adding weight to his big frame and may not be ready for college heavyweights yet but he should be an exciting wrestler to watch develop. Seventeen PSU wrestlers are registered to compete in the event today while five others stay behind in State College as they prepare for the NWCA All Star Classic on Tuesday evening in Rec Hall. C.J. item.title: Manchester City's torrid winless run in the Premier League extended to four games on Saturday afternoon as yet another lacklustre display from Enzo Maresca's men saw the Blues draw 1-1 with Fulham at the Etihad Stadium.
item.description: Manchester City's torrid winless run in the Premier League extended to four games on Saturday afternoon as yet another lacklustre display from Enzo Maresca's men saw the Blues draw 1-1 with Fulham at the Etihad Stadium. How does Enzo Maresca fix Manchester City's defence? A City performace that was, for large parts, void of intensity and creativity, saw the Blues fail to beat Fulham at the Etihad Stadium for the first time in 15 years, dating back to February 2011 under Roberto Mancini. There was hope that, after the international break, those of a sky-blue persuasion would be galvanised to right the wrongs of their recent shortcomings, having suffered three consecutive league defeats; unfortunately, however, it was more of the slothful same. In the opening exchanges, Maresca's men struggled to ride the storm of Fulham 's intensity but did conjure some somewhat presentable chances early on, with Erling Haaland seeing his effort thwarted by David Affengruber whilst a deflection steered Nico O'Reilly's shot narrowly wide. However, with just 16 minutes on the clock, Manchester City 's defensive frailties reared their ugly head once again as the Cottagers drew first blood in the tie through Rodrigo Muniz, who latched on to a superb pass from former Blue Oscar Bobb and hammered past Gianluigi Donnarumma to give the visitors the lead. Just eight minutes later, the home side thought they had restored parity after an excellent cross from Iliman Ndiaye found Haaland, and the 26-year-old, after squandering the initial chance, seized upon a goalkeeping mishap by Bernd Leno, prodding home after the German appeared to spill the ball. But referee Thomas Bramall, controversially brought the celebrations to an abrupt halt, having adjudged that the former Arsenal shot-stopper had two hands on the ball at the time of the Norwegian's follow-up, resulting in a foul and disallowed goal. Subsequently, a defensive blunder from O'Reilly nearly proved calamitous as the Englishman allowed Bobb to snatch possession inside the Manchester City area, but Donnarumma was on hand to spare his teammate's blushes and deny the Fulham number 14. After a dismal first 45 which saw the halftime whistle met with jeers from the Etihad Stadium crowd, Maresca was in dire need of an injection of impetus into his side, and 12 minutes after the restart, Elliott Anderson obliged, producing a sumptuous volley which nestled into the back of the Fulham net and hauled the hosts level. Whilst the goal certainly did breathe some life into the home side, City were still by no means at their scintillating best in the second period, with the lack of ideas and desire remaining a glaringly obvious issue. In truth, Fulham looked more likely to walk away with three points, but Donnarumma, whose shot-stopping was much improved, remained resolute, preventing both Muniz and Calvin Bassey from deciding the tie late on. In the end, the Blues had to settle for a dispiriting point, which sees them trail league le

item.title: Coco Gauff Explains Why Dad Corey Was Missing From Her Player Box Despite Family’s Presence at BJK Cup Play-offs
item.description: Coco Gauff Image via Instagram/@cocogauff Coco Gauff explained her father, Corey Gauff’s, absence from her player box during the Billie Jean King Cup play-offs in her hometown. Following her exit from the WTA Finals, Gauff led Team USA against Hungary in the BJK Cup. She locked horns with Dalma Galfi on Saturday, November 21, 2026, in Delray Beach, Florida. Gauff overwhelmed Galfi from the baseline and saw off her opponent 6-1, 6-1. Gauff was seen being cheered by her mother, Candi, grandmother Yvonne Lee Odom, and her brothers. However, her father was nowhere to be seen in her player’s box. The United States Tennis Association shared a video of her family supporting her and wrote: “Coco Gauff’s family is bringing the hometown support!” The video did not feature her father. Gauff shared the video on her Instagram story and revealed that her father was watching her compete from a different spot around the court. “My dad watches from the back lolll,” Gauff wrote. Screenshot of Coco Gauff’s Instagram story. Coco Gauff’s father was her initial tennis coach. He used to watch his daughter compete from the player’s box. However, in 2023, Corey Gauff decided to move elsewhere in the stadium. Coco Gauff reveals amusing story about her father missing her US Open winning moment After Coco Gauff’s third-round win at the 2026 Australian Open, an interviewer asked Gauff about her father and from where he watches her matches. Gauff revealed that it is always the other people who inform her from where her father is watching her compete. She stated that her father struggles to control his emotions during matches and hence she has asked him not to sit in her player box. “No, it’s other people who tell me (where he is),” she told reporters. “Yeah, the reason why is he can’t control his reactions. It’s not necessarily for me but for him. I told him, ‘We’ve just got to cut it.'” (via Reuters ) Coco Gauff further highlighted the 2023 US Open incident, where she won her first Grand Slam title by seeing off Aryna Sabalenka. The American tennis player’s father was in the stadium gym when she clinched the winning point. An attendant had to inform him of her victory after which he rushed to congratulate her. “I heard when I won the U.S. Open he was in the gym, and the TV was behind so the gym attendant had to tell him I actually won. So he needed to run out and greet me in the crowd. I don’t know where he was at French Open and you probably know more than I do, but yeah, I’ve heard that he’s all around the site, usually like locked in on the screen and just pacing,” Coco Gauff added. Gauff won her second Grand Slam title at the 2025 French Open. item.title: “Fireable Offense for Matt Campbell”: Brandon Walker Blasts Penn State HC After Meltdown vs. Rutgers
item.description: Matt Campbell During a Press Conference © Imagn Penn State head coach Matt Campbell was put on the hot seat by Barstool Sports’ Brandon Walker following the Nittany Lions’ 25-24 loss to Rutgers on Saturday. The Nittany Lions entered the matchup as clear favorites against a Rutgers team that had won just two games all season. However, the Scarlet Knights ultimately blew Penn State’s two-score lead. After the game, Walker called out Campbell for the loss against Rutgers, deeming it a fireable offense. “I honestly think that might be a fireable offense for Matt Campbell at Penn State. You can’t ever lose to Rutgers,” Walker wrote on X. Penn State had led 16-0 and later held a 24-10 advantage with less than 11 minutes remaining. Rutgers pulled off a stunning comeback. Rutgers running back Antwan Raymond caught a pass short of the goal line and lateraled to wide receiver Ben Black III, who scored on the final play of regulation. Rutgers converted the ensuing two-point attempt to take a 25-24 lead. Time ran out before Penn State could reply. The loss against Rutgers was particularly damaging because it ended Penn State’s 18-game winning streak against the Scarlet Knights. Penn State last lost in 1988. HC Matt Campbell Takes Responsibility for Penn State’s Collapse In his post-game conference, Penn State head coach Matt Campbell took responsibility for the loss to Rutgers. “I didn’t have us prepared to play our best football game, Senior Day, the end of the season, and that really hurts me, and it puts a lot of responsibility on my shoulders,” Campbell said via Go PSU Sports. “To me, our ability to do hard things is still keeping this team from becoming its best.” Campbell added that the team has failed to be excellent for the full 60 minutes, leading to poor finishes in several games. Previously, the Nittany Lions failed to close the game against Wisconsin. On Saturday, they allowed Rutgers 15 unanswered points. Penn State quarterback Rocco Becht and running back Cam Wallace committed two costly fumbles in the loss. As a result, the Nittany Lions could only manage 26 yards of offense in the fourth quarter. Penn State entered the matchup against Rutgers after recording three straight wins. They had the momentum and were making progress under Campbell before the latest heartbreaking loss. Penn State fell to 6-5 overall and 3-5 in Big Ten play. The Nittany Lions will conclude their regular season against Maryland on November 28. item.title: “This Is Disgusting”: CFB Analyst Questions Kyle Whittingham’s “Respect” for Women & “Lack of Accountability” After HC’s Comments on Andrew Marsh’s Suspension
item.description: Kyle Whittingham © Imagn Images College football analyst Liam Blutman criticized Michigan Wolverines head coach Kyle Whittingham after he deemed Andrew Marsh’s one-game suspension for his alleged incident with a female food delivery driver “fair.” Marsh allegedly exposed himself to a female food delivery driver on Feb. 2, 2026, in Pittsfield Township, Michigan. The sophomore is facing a misdemeanor indecent exposure charge. “*Allegedly* Exposing your genitals to your food delivery girl = one game suspension,” Blutman wrote on X. “Does Coach Whittingham not respect women? I don’t stand with this and am flabbergasted at the lack of accountability. This is DISGUSTING!!” The incident came to light two days before Michigan’s 18-16 triple-overtime victory over No. 4 UCLA on Saturday. Whittingham wouldn’t discuss the details of the case, but said the suspension was fair. “We thought it warranted a game suspension, and Andrew agreed,” Whittingham told reporters. “Can’t say much about the case, but it’s unfortunate; it’s bad judgment. I think a one-game suspension was probably very fair to put behind us.” Meanwhile, Michigan said it had only recently learned about the incident and would continue monitoring the situation. “We were just made aware of an incident involving Andrew Marsh,” the school stated via MLive’s Aaron McMann on Thursday . “We will continue to monitor the situation as more information becomes available, but we are unable to comment further due to the ongoing case.” Kyle Whittingham Expects Andrew Marsh to Return Against Ohio State Andrew Marsh is one of Michigan’s leading wide receivers this season. He has the most receptions (48), accounting for 459 yards and one touchdown. Michigan would like to have him on the field when it faces Ohio State next week. Kyle Whittingham confirmed that the school is expecting the sophomore wide receiver to return for the game against the Buckeyes. “That’s the plan, to be determined. It’s still an ongoing process, if new things come to light. But as we sit here tonight, I would expect that he’d be back next week,” Whittingham told reporters (via On3) . Marsh is scheduled to appear in court on Dec. 2, four days after Michigan’s regular-season finale against Ohio State. item.title: Mikel Arteta confirms major Arsenal injury blow after Newcastle United clash
item.description: Mikel Arteta confirms major Arsenal injury blow after Newcastle United clash David Raya Injury Concern Clouds Arsenal After Newcastle Draw Arsenal left St James’ Park with a point, but the bigger issue is in goal. David Raya, one of the key reasons behind Arsenal’s strong opening to the season, went off injured in the 2-2 draw with Newcastle and now faces scans on a suspected shoulder problem. The sequence was straightforward enough. Raya collided with William Osula while trying to release the ball, went down in clear discomfort and needed treatment on the pitch. He could not continue. He walked off, headed straight down the tunnel and that will worry Arsenal far more than the dropped points. There is no need to dress it up. If Raya is out, it is a problem. He has been reliable, calm and productive, with seven clean sheets in Arsenal’s first ten Premier League games. That sort of consistency matters, particularly for a side heading into a run that can shape its season. Photo IMAGO Mikel Arteta Awaits David Raya Scan Results Mikel Arteta offered no certainty after the match, saying: “Unfortunately, he had to come off, which is not good news. “He will have an MRI assessment tomorrow, but at the moment I don’t know.” He added: “It was a knock, I don’t know how it happened and what the injury is at the moment. We have to wait and see tomorrow. “We know how important David is for us. Tomorrow we will have more news.” Arsenal Fixtures Make Raya Injury More Serious Kepa Arrizabalaga replaced Raya for the final 20 minutes, entering with Arsenal 2-1 down. By full-time it had finished 2-2, though the result quickly became secondary. Arsenal had led at the break through Eberechi Eze, then lost control after half-time as Newcastle turned the game. Now comes the difficult part. Arsenal host Manchester City next weekend, with Real Madrid, Tottenham and Manchester United also on the schedule before Christmas. If Raya misses any part of that spell, Arsenal’s margin for error shrinks. There is enough quality in the squad, but goalkeeper injuries are different. You do not rotate calm, command and trust so easily.

item.title: Watford sack boss Dionisi after 18 games
item.description: Alessio Dionisi was the fifth Italian manager hired by Watford under the ownership of the Pozzo family [Getty Images] Watford are looking for their sixth manager in 18 months after they sacked head coach Alessio Dionisi following 18 games in charge. The 46-year-old Italian was appointed in June after the departure of Ed Still, who himself lasted only three months at Vicarage Road. Still, Javi Gracia and Paulo Pezzolano were all also given full-time contracts after Tom Cleverley left in May 2025. Dionisi was Watford's 12th head coach, not including interim bosses, since the end of the 2020-21 season, and leaves the Hornets searching for a 25th since the Pozzo family took over the club in 2012. The club have had 57 permanent managers in their 145-year history. The decision to replace him comes after Saturday's crushing 4-0 defeat by Sheffield United at Bramall Lane. Dionisi's dismissal caps an underwhelming start to the season, with the Hornets having won just four league games to leave them 21st in the table. "We thank Alessio and his staff for his professionalism and their efforts," sporting director Luke Dowling told the club website. "As I'm sure the supporters have seen, Alessio is a really good guy and we wish him the best for the future. "The process has started for a replacement and we hope to be in a position to announce that shortly." Dionisi was sacked by Serie B club Empoli in March after only five months in charge following a run of five wins in 22 matches. His spell in charge of the Hornets was his first outside his homeland and started promisingly when his youthful side beat Southampton in their opening league game. But they won only two of their next 12 in all competitions, and despite deservedly beating Charlton on 17 October, reverses at Wolves and Norwich followed, before four points from Dionisi's final three games in charge of the Hertfordshire side and his dismissal means further upheaval for the Hornets. With more than a third of the league season complete, Watford are one place outside of the Championship relegation zone (table shown before Burnley face Blackburn on Sunday) [BBC] Since sacking Cleverley at the end of the 2024-25 campaign, the club has now been through four permanent head coaches, as well as interim boss Charlie Daniels' two-game spell in charge. Of those four, only Gracia, in his second spell at Vicarage Road, took charge of more than 20 games. On the morning of their final-day drubbing by Coventry last season, chief executive Scott Duxbury wrote a statement on the club website saying Watford had made mistakes, labelling their end to the campaign "unacceptable" and "truly disappointing in the extreme". item.title: 'I fulfilled a dream!' - Leandro Paredes reacts to winning silverware as Juan Roman Riquelme lands first title as Boca Juniors president
item.description: Atletico Mineiro v Boca Juniors - Copa CONMEBOL Sudamericana 2026 Final - Getty Images Sport Leandro Paredes celebrated a dream fulfilled as Boca Juniors beat Atletico Mineiro 2-0 to win a record third Copa Sudamericana title and hand Juan Roman Riquelme his first international trophy as president. Their triumph in Barranquilla ended an 18-year continental wait for the club. Paredes celebrates as Riquelme claims first title Boca Juniors defeated Atletico Mineiro 2-0 at the Estadio Metropolitano Roberto Melendez in Barranquilla to become the first three-time Copa Sudamericana champions. Santiago Ascacibar opened the scoring in the 16th minute before Miguel Merentiel struck three minutes into the second half. The victory ended Boca's 18-year wait for an international trophy since the 2008 Recopa and gave club president Juan Roman Riquelme his first continental crown as an executive. Having won three Copa Libertadores titles in Boca's number 10 shirt as a player, Riquelme now shares continental silverware with the Xeneize from the directors' box. Paredes hails dream title after returning home Leandro Paredes captained and drove Boca's campaign after returning to the club, leading CONMEBOL competitions in 2026 with 791 completed passes, 234 final-third passes and 212 line-breaking passes. Speaking to ESPN after the final whistle, Paredes shared his emotion at winning silverware back in Azul y Oro . "I fulfilled a dream," Paredes said. "I always dreamed of being able to win a title. I only have words of gratitude for the club. Thanks to my children, my family and my friends. Since I was little, I've been taught to compete and win everything possible. I love winning and competing. I'm lucky to achieve important things." Riquelme's mid-year reset and Villa's impact After finishing third in Copa Libertadores Group D, Boca pivoted in June under Riquelme's leadership by appointing former team-mate Rodolfo Arruabarrena as head coach and bringing in players including Sebastian Villa, who assisted Merentiel's second-half goal in Barranquilla. Back in March at the CONMEBOL group draw, Riquelme had already spoken of the pull of continental football , saying: "Playing in the Copa always creates excitement, both in the squad and among our fans." Villa also highlighted his joy after helping Boca past O'Higgins, Deportivo Recoleta, Sao Paulo and Vasco da Gama on the way to the final. "I'm very happy, thank God it happened, returning to the club that gave me the opportunity," Villa told ESPN. "I came back with great enthusiasm and a desire for a title. I've won two in a row." Libertadores return and Recopa await in 2027 Lifting the Copa Sudamericana brings a USD 10,000,000 champions' prize and direct entry into the 2027 Copa Libertadores group stage without qualifying rounds. Boca also earn a berth in the 2027 Recopa against the winner of the November 28 Libertadores final between Palmeiras and Estudiantes de La Plata. With the Argentine Cup and domestic league stil

item.title: Gameday column: Bills and the current state of strength of schedule
item.description: It’s like each week there’s arisen a new narrative about this Buffalo Bills team. Leading into Week 11 against the Dolphins, it was all about strength of schedule… probably because of Buffalo’s competition — or lack thereof — since the bye week. I’ll be the first to mention that teams are not always what their record says they are. But what these Bills are doing is subtly different from previous Bills teams during the Josh Allen era. What has remained the same is Buffalo’s regular-season dominance. Since 2020, the Bills have been the NFL’s best team in the regular season. They have the most wins and the highest point differential by an insane margin. But like I wrote a week ago, the Sean McDermott clubs always had an uncharacteristic stumble or two during said regular season that kept them away out of the No. 1 seat in the AFC playoffs. Of course today, against the Dolphins, represents one of those “stumble” possibilities with the colossal clash on Thanksgiving against the Chiefs looming. But that’s the not the crux of this column. Are the Bills the best 8-1 team in NFL history? No. Are they the best 8-1 team in the past decade. No. But they’ve done exactly what a team should do against the competition level it has faced. Regarding the aforementioned point differential, it’s my absolute favorite measure of team quality… because it’s straightforward and pretty darn predictive. How’s this for point differential’s stickiness — 11 of the past 12 Super Bowl winners finished the regular season in the Top 6 in point differential. Insane, right? From 2004 – 2025, 17 of 22 of the clubs that hoisted the Lombardi Trophy at season’s end were a Top 6 point-differential team during the regular season. And this Bills team enters this AFC East game against the Dolphins second in point differential, at +88. If Buffalo had been squeaking by lesser opponents regularly, I’d be the first to write their 8-1 feels phony. That hasn’t been the case whatsoever. And teams can only play the opponents on their schedule. Among the nine teams at 7-2 or better right now, only the Broncos (.583) and Vikings (.518) have faced a cumulative opponent win percentage above .500. The Bills are third on that list at .480, as their opponents have a combined record of 40-47. The combined record of Chiefs’ opponents to date is 34-53 (.391). They’re currently in last in that metric. (another shoutout to Jeremy White from WGR550 who noticed this earlier this week.) Oh, and as for the strength-of-schedule element that legitimately matters come playoff-seeding time — the Bills currently have the second-best strength of victory at .455, behind only the Broncos, the sole AFC club with a strength of victory over .500. On this note, the first half of the 2026 NFL season has shown a more sizable gap between the great teams and the noticeably bad ones. Ahead of Week 11, nine teams with seven or more wins is the most in any season in the NFL since at least 2001. Eight clubs with seven or more losses

item.title: 'Verstappen's race craft should make Mercedes worry ahead of 2027'
item.description: The 1997 F1 world champion, Jacques Villeneuve , believes Max Verstappen 's race craft could pose a serious threat to the Mercedes drivers ahead of the 2027 Formula 1 season. Speaking on Sky Sports, the Canadian enjoyed the show with so many overtakes at the Las Vegas Grand Prix . He said: "It was exciting! People will say 'there was a battery involved' [in all the passes], but it doesn't matter." According to Villeneuve, who was full of praise for Verstappen, today's events should serve as a major warning for Mercedes. "We saw some race craft. Max was above and the two Mercedes drivers were lacking in that respect and what it is telling us is that unless next year Mercedes have a car that's superior, they can't win because there's something missing." Villeneuve points out two other world champions alongside Verstappen Villeneuve was also positive about what he saw from the two British world champion on the grid today, Lewis Hamilton and Lando Norris . "You could see that Lewis had good race craft as well, Lando. It was really fun to see. "We saw today a race where you don't need pit stops, you don't need tyres that degrade. We had a race where drivers could push like qualy laps all the time and that allowed them to race. It was great fun," he concluded. Max Verstappen praised for his intelligence during the race - Photo: RacePictures Max Verstappen praised for his intelligence during the race - Photo: RacePictures Verstappen takes aim at Russell after his victory in Las Vegas Speaking after the race, Verstappen could not resist taking a jab at Russell. He said : "It's not like a success today. The thing is he speaks a lot next to the track. And honestly, for me it doesn't really bother me because he's so far below my level that it doesn't really make any sense for me anyway to try and challenge that. So, it doesn't bother me. And today, karma is a b****. "It was honestly fantastic when I looked in my mirror and I saw what's happening. So I was like, fantastic. My day is only getting better. And of course, when I then crossed the line in first, my day was complete."

item.title: Commentary: A salute to Elyjah Staples and other football stars who stay dedicated to same school
item.description: Receiver and linebacker Elyjah Staples stayed for four years at Marquez and leaves in January to play for California. (Steve Galluzzo / For The Times) Because it has become rare for a top high school athlete to stay at the same school for four years, let’s take a moment to salute football players who ignored the agents sending text messages trying to get them to move and weren’t swayed by the constant wooing of parents seeking to buy a championship team with their wallet. These are the players who simply bet on themselves and trusted the process. It starts with a standing ovation for Elyjah Staples , a 6-foot-3, 210-pound senior at Marquez High in Huntington Park. If anyone were to become a target to steal, it would be Staples. “You can’t get better in the City Section.” “You can’t get exposure in the City Section.” “You can’t get prepared for college in the City Section.” Read more: High school football: Top performers in the Southland Yes, it’s absolute nonsense, proven again by what Staples accomplished in four years of loyalty to Marquez. “He put us on the map,” coach Rudy Fortiz said. He has a scholarship waiting for him at California when he graduates this semester and arrives at Berkeley in January. “I thought I was going to lose him,” Fortiz said in what has become almost a yearly waiting game among football coaches seeing if their top player will be swooped away by the promises from the many recruiters for private and public schools who never get caught even though recruiting is illegal in high school sports. What kept Staples at Marquez was his love for his school, confidence in defensive coordinator Greg Tucker, who has known Staples for years, and his motivation to prove he could earn a scholarship out of Marquez. Elyjah Staples is a standout middle linebacker and tight end for Marquez. (Eric Sondheimer / Los Angeles Times) “You don’t have to go to a big school to play if you have the grades and go to work,” Fortiz said. That will be Staples’ legacy at Marquez as his name appears on TV screens in the coming years playing college football. He was recruited to California to be a defensive end, but he’s being used as a middle linebacker and tight end for Marquez because that’s where the team needs him. He will do anything to help his team succeed. Here's the City Section finals schedule. Saturday at L.A. item.title: Former All-Star has created NBA’s biggest ‘f–king mess’ — and it just keeps getting worse
item.description: Dejounte Murray #5 of the New Orleans Pelicans reacts to a call during a game against the Denver Nuggets in New Orleans, Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026. Situations don’t get much uglier than Dejounte Murray’s in New Orleans. The Pelicans guard wants a trade from the franchise , and his relationship with the organization appears beyond repair. But worst of all, opposing teams reportedly aren’t biting, asking for draft compensation just to take him off New Orleans’ hands in a trade. “What a f–king mess,” one NBA executive told Yahoo Sports’ Kelly Iko this week . “No one wants to touch him.” Dejounte Murray #5 of the New Orleans Pelicans reacts to a call during a game against the Denver Nuggets in New Orleans, Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026. Getty Images It’s a quick fall for the former All-Star, whom the Pelicans acquired from the Hawks in a 2024 blockbuster deal for a package that included Dyson Daniels and two first-round picks. Now, just over two years later, the Pelicans could be forced to give up even more assets to get rid of him. Two opposing team officials told Sports Illustrated’s Chris Mannix they would demand a first-round pick to take on Murray’s contract, which pays him $32.8 million this season and includes a $30.8 million player option for 2027-28. Murray, 30, has appeared in just 54 games since arriving in New Orleans, having suffered a broken hand and a torn Achilles. Dejounte Murray of the New Orleans Pelicans reacts during a game against the Golden State Warriors in San Francisco, Monday, Nov. 9, 2026. Getty Images He’s averaging 13.4 points and 4.4 assists through nine games this season, shooting just 29.6 percent from beyond the arc. But his struggles on the court are only part of the problem. Murray took to social media to lash out at critics earlier this month, suggesting someone within the organization was responsible for negative posts about him. Dejounte Murray of the New Orleans Pelicans handles the ball against the LA Clippers on Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026, at Intuit Dome in Inglewood, Calif. NBAE via Getty Images “The sabotage is real!” he wrote in a since-deleted post. In another since-deleted tirade, Murray went after a Pelicans fan account that highlighted his mistakes during a blowout loss to the Nets. “You have no f–king clue what we dealing with,” Murray, who hasn’t played since Nov. 11, wrote on the platform. ESPN’s Brian Windhorst subsequently claimed the Pelicans had sent Murray home following his trade request, while suggesting the guard had become difficult to keep around the team. “They sent him home,” Windhorst said on “The Hoop Collective” podcast. item.title: “A Lot to Learn”: Fernando Mendoza Makes Frank Admission on First Raiders Start in Loss to Seahawks
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, IN – FEBRUARY 27: Indiana quarterback Fernando Mendoza answers questions from the media during the NFL, American Football Herren, USA Scouting Combine on February 27, 2026 at the Indiana Convention Center in Indianapolis, IN. Photo by Zach Bolinger/Icon Sportswire NFL: FEB 27 Scouting Combine EDITORIAL USE ONLY Icon2602270203 ©IMAGO/Icon Sportswire It’s rare for NFL players to maintain a LinkedIn profile. Even if they do, hardly do they update about what’s going on in their professional life regularly. But Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza has always been that sincere kid, maintaining an updated LinkedIn profile. In his latest post, the 2026 draft No.1 pick shared his promotion update. “Promoted ????,” wrote Mendoza . “A lot to learn from my first NFL start. Grateful for my family, friends, and Raider Nation for the support! Looking forward to getting better and earning the trust of my teammates and coaches every day.” When the Raiders drafted the Heisman winner, they had some plans in store. After drafting Mendoza, ever since the beginning of the 2026 season, Las Vegas was not ready to hand the starting reins to veteran Kirk Cousins throughout the season. While Cousins started nine games for the Raiders this season, they traded the veteran to the Minnesota Vikings on November 10 in exchange for a 2027 third-round NFL Draft pick. That’s when the golden opportunity came for Mendoza. “It’s something that [Mendoza] worked very hard for since the moment he walked into this building,” Raiders general manager John Spytek said. “He passed every test. I want to stop short of saying he’s earned it, but he put us in a position where we had to make a really hard decision today with his growth as a person, as a teammate, as a leader, as a quarterback.” Rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza's honest reflection on his NFL debut reveals the steep learning curve ahead. Subscribe to stay updated on his development and the Raiders' quarterback future. Fernando Mendoza had the picture-perfect resume to pitch himself in the pro league. Playing his last season with the Indiana Hoosiers, he led Indiana to a 16-0 record and a National Championship. He also joined an elite club, becoming one of the 18 players in college football history to win two honors in the same season: the Heisman Trophy and National Championship. Trying to document all of Mendoza’s college records would be a lengthy exercise. His accomplishments include setting Indiana’s single-season record with 41 passing touchdowns, posting a program-best 95.0% completion rate in a single game, and recording the highest passing efficiency in the FBS during the 2025 season at 182.9. Those are just some of the numbers that highlight his college success. However, Las Vegas did not trust him immediately based on his college stint. item.title: Verstappen Says Russell Is ‘So Far Below My Level’ and Hints Vegas Was Karma
item.description: Max Verstappen said George Russell is “so far below my level” after winning the Las Vegas Grand Prix, and called Russell’s late mistake karma. The two clashed at Turn 14 in final practice on Friday, Nov. 20, and the stewards gave Verstappen a warning for erratic driving. Asked about it in the FIA press conference after qualifying, Verstappen said only, “Nothing happened.” Russell went further, telling Sky Sports Italy that Verstappen does it “week in, week out with many drivers” and that “somebody’s got to stand up to that guy.” There was no drama on Lap 1 of the race on Saturday night, when they started side by side on the front row. They swapped the lead several times, and their race-long battle never got dangerous. With Andrea Kimi Antonelli in the mix toward the end, it ended badly for Russell. Running third behind Verstappen and his Mercedes teammate Antonelli, Russell tried to retake second into Turn 5 three laps from the end. He ran off line and over debris, seemingly from Isack Hadjar’s car, locked up and went head-on into the barrier, according to F1 . He rejoined and finished ninth . “I could have been conservative and I would probably have come home P3,” Russell said. Max Verstappen leads Red Bull teammate Isack Hadjar in the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Nov. 21, 2026. Image Credit: Mark Thompson/Getty Images via Red Bull Content Pool Verstappen Goes Unfiltered on Russell In the FIA press conference after the race, Verstappen was asked whether Russell’s comments had been on his mind and whether it was nice to get one up on him. “Well, I mean, it’s not like it’s like a success today,” said Verstappen. “I mean, the thing is, he speaks a lot next to the track. And honestly, for me, it doesn’t really bother me because he’s so far below my level that it doesn’t really make any sense for me anyway to try and challenge that, so it doesn’t bother me. “And today karma is a b**ch. It was honestly fantastic when I looked in my mirror, and I saw what was happening. So, I was like, ‘fantastic, my day is only getting better’. And of course, when I then crossed the line in first, my day was complete.” Verstappen didn’t spell out what he saw in his mirror, but he was leading when Russell went off at Turn 5. Verstappen Pulls Away in the Fight for Second Max Verstappen lifts the winner’s trophy on the podium after the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Nov. 21, 2026. Image Credit: Clive Rose/Getty Images via Red Bull Content Pool The win, Verstappen’s fourth of the season, took him to 304 points, second in the drivers’ standings behind champion Antonelli. Lewis Hamilton is third on 267, and Russell and Lando Norris are tied on 264, so Verstappen heads into the last two races, in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, 40 points clear of Russell in the fight to finish runner-up. item.title: Jürgen Klopp ‘happy’ with Germany drawing Belgium in the Nations League
item.description: Photo by Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images | Getty Images After strong showing in the UEFA Nations League, Jürgen Klopp led Germany to the quarterfinals where they will face Belgium. The 59-year-old coach said he’s happy with the draw and profiled his team’s opponents. “I’m happy with the draw. I’m looking forward to facing Belgium. They’re a strong opponent, and they also have a new manager,” Klopp said (as captured by X account @iMiaSanMia ). “They had a great Nations League campaign, and I know several of their players very well. Kevin De Bruyne is one of the greatest players the Premier League has ever seen. And he’s still good – unfortunately. We’re fully aware that we’re right at the beginning of a development process. We want to carry this positive atmosphere forward, but there’s still a lot of work to do.” The last time the two sides met in 2023, Belgium won 3-2 which was their first victory over the Germans since 1954. item.title: Houston high school football: Takeaways and top performers from area playoffs
item.description: La Porte running back Sean Simon rushed for 458 yards and seven touchdowns on Friday. (Jason Fochtman/Houston Chronicle) From dazzling running back performances to eye-opening wins, the second round of the Texas high school football playoffs provided plenty to talk about. Here's a look at some of the key takeaways and top performers. Simon scores seven touchdowns La Porte running back Sean Simon has been a prolific ball carrier for the Bulldogs since his freshman year. But what he accomplished on Friday night at Tomball ISD Stadium was certainly his best performance yet. The junior four-star recruit rushed for a program-record 458 yards and seven touchdowns on 41 carries during a 63-49 win over College Station in the Class 5A Division I bracket. Six of those touchdowns came in the first half. Simon's performance earned him two more entries in the Houston high school football record book . He now tied with several other players for second place in the single-game touchdown category. His yardage against College Station also ranks as the eighth-highest single-game total and gives him a career-high 2,547 for the season. With 6,340 career rushing yards, Simon now ranks 13th in Houston high school football history. With his output against College Station, he passed Katy's Deondrick Glass, Pearland's Anthony Evans and Tomball's Bubba Greeley. La Porte (10-2) will take on Angleton (11-1) in the regional semifinals at 7 p.m. Friday at Freedom field. College Park, Klein rally for wins College Park and Klein were both on the brink of elimination Friday night. But the Cavaliers and Bearkats kept fighting and ultimately mounted late comebacks to keep their seasons alive for at least one more week. College Park (9-3) trailed Langham Creek by two scores in the third quarter before finishing the game with 16 unanswered points to pull out a 28-21 victory in the Class 6A Division II bracket. Kaylen Stephens had a big game on the ground for the Cavaliers, rushing for 188 yards and two touchdowns on 28 carries. Antonio Booker added 91 yards on 15 carries as College Park rushed for 303 as a team and secured its second straight trip to the third round. College Park will battle No. 1 state-ranked North Crowley (12-0) at 7 p.m. Friday at Waco ISD Stadium. Klein (11-1), meanwhile, trailed 27-10 against The Woodlands in the third quarter before making a furious rally to win 31-27. Kendrick Brown scored the go-ahead touchdown on a 1-yard run with 1:30 remaining, sending the Bearkats to the third round of the playoffs for the first time since 2009 when the program reached the semifinals. Klein will take on Waxahachie (11-1) at 2 p.m. Saturday at Waco ISD Stadium. Katy continues dominance Katy continued its dominant season with a 47-7 victory in a true road game against Hutto in the Class 6A Division I bracket Friday night.
