item.title: Skip Bayless says he has seen a player who’s going to cause ‘more problems’ for Victor Wembanyama
item.description: Photo by Ronald Cortes/Getty Images Victor Wembanyama is arguably the best player in the NBA right now. The Frenchman scored 50 points in 32 minutes in the San Antonio Spurs’ 114-91 win against the New Orleans Pelicans on Saturday. Before that even happened, Skip Bayless watched the Oklahoma City Thunder in action, and he was very impressed with one player: Aday Mara. Skip Bayless says Aday Mara will cause ‘more and more problems’ for Victor Wembanyama When Wembanyama is in full flow, it’s almost impossible to stop him. The Spurs star, still only 22, possesses all the traits you would want in a big man, and he uses his physical advantages perfectly to get the job done. But when people saw the Thunder draft Aday Mara in the summer, the Spaniard quickly earned the nickname ‘Wemby stopper’ for his size and ability. Bayless called Mara the ‘antidote’ to Wembanyama many months ago, and now, the TV personality has heaped more praise on him. After watching his performance against the Pelicans in the NBA Cup, where he scored 22 points and recorded 16 rebounds in 29 minutes, Bayless made a claim about Mara and Wembanyama. He tweeted : “Aday Mara (22/16/3 blocks) is arriving for the Thunder. He’s obviously no Wemby, but he will soon be causing more and more problems for Wemby – as he did here and there on Opening Night in San Antonio.” What happened when Aday Mara faced Victor Wembanyama? Mara and Wembanyama faced each other when the OKC Thunder took on the San Antonio Spurs on the opening night of the new NBA season. The rookie came off the bench for the Thunder in the third quarter and immediately made an impact, blocking a Wembanyama dunk attempt. Then, the former Michigan star finished a two-handed alley-oop slam at the other end to help OKC gain momentum and eventually win the game. Mara’s block to deny Wembanyama made a lot of headlines, which is why all eyes will be on the duo when they face each other again in February. We can’t wait to see who will win that match-up. item.title: How Lee Trevino reacted to Phil Mickelson’s scathing criticism of Tom Watson after the 2014 Ryder Cup
item.description: Photo by BEN STANSALL / AFP via Getty Images Phil Mickelson caused uproar in 2014 after he very publicly criticized the 2014 US Ryder Cup captain, Tom Watson. Mickelson has always been regarded as one of the most outspoken players on the professional golfing scene. And he certainly lived up to his reputation back in 2014 after the United States were comfortably beaten by Team Europe at the Ryder Cup. During the press conference after the United States’ Ryder Cup defeat to Europe, Phil Mickelson was asked to put his finger on what went wrong at Gleneagles. The now 56-year-old took a swipe at Tom Watson ‘s refusal to stick to Paul Azinger’s ‘pod system’ that worked to excellent effect during the 2008 Ryder Cup at Valhalla. “ There were two things that allow us to play our best, I think, that Paul Azinger did, and one was he got everybody invested in the process, “ Mickelson explained. “ He got everybody invested in who they were going to play with, who the picks were going to be, who was going to be in their pod, who — when they would play, and they had a great leader for each pod. In my case, we had Ray Floyd, and we hung out together and we were all invested in each other’s play. We were invested in picking Hunter that week; Anthony Kim and myself and Justin were in a pod, and we were involved on having Hunter be our guy to fill our pod. So we were invested in the process. “ And the other thing that Paul did really well was he had a great game plan for us, you know, how we were going to go about doing this. How we were going to go about playing together; golf ball, format, what we were going to do, if so-and-so is playing well, if so-and-so is not playing well, we had a real game plan. Those two things helped us bring out our best golf. “ We use that same process in The Presidents Cup and we do really well. Unfortunately, we have strayed from a winning formula in 2008 for the last three Ryder Cups, and we need to consider maybe getting back to that formula that helped us play our best. “ Mickelson’s comments drew audible gasps from the press room and the tension in the room was palpable. The six-time major champion had just openly criticized the captaincy methods of one of the greatest golfers ever to have played the game. The interesting point here is that Mickelson’s criticism of Watson was perfectly valid. Everything he said made perfect sense. However, Lee Trevino did not see it that way at all. How Lee Trevino reacted to Phil Mickelson’s criticism of Tom Watson Back in 2015, Trevino was asked how he felt about Mickelson’s criticism of Watson after the Ryder Cup at Gleneagles the previous year. The six-time major champion did not hold back when defending his good friend, as quoted by The Golf Channel . “I thought it would have come out a lot better from someone like Patrick Reed, who went 3-0-1, instead of a guy who has been a part of so many losing teams,” Trevino said. “If I had a losing record in the Ryder Cup, I’d keep my mouth shut. “Tom

item.title: Predicting College Football Playoff field after Week 12: BYU, Indiana fall out
item.description: Week 12 of college football had a very weak slate of games — on paper. However, as we’ve seen all season, there were several key upsets. Parity has been the theme of college football this season and it’s going to be hard for the College Football Playoff committee to determine who deserves to be ranked 10th and 11th going into Tuesday night. Getting back to the upsets, the biggest ones took place in the Big Ten. Previously unbeaten UCLA fell to Michigan on the road . The Bruins lost in three overtimes, and the kicker was that Bob Chesney’s team potentially lost backup quarterback Ty Dieffenbach, who was carted off the field during overtime. Indiana fell to Washington on the road, and the Hoosiers have looked very mortal all season. IU struggles to score the ball, and Curt Cignetti turned back to Josh Hoover in the second half, hoping he would spark the struggling offense. Turns out, the Huskies got a major in — also in overtime. Then there was Ohio State. The Buckeyes were a big winner this past week in the playoff rankings, moving up to No. 14. Ohio State could’ve beaten both Nebraska and Michigan and earned its way into the playoff. But a shocking 31-28 loss to the Cornhuskers effectively eliminated Ryan Day’s team . In other news, BYU needed three overtimes to take down a bad Kansas team, and Miami was taken to the brink against Virginia Tech, but the Hurricanes came out on top. Here’s how the CFP field might look after Week 12. item.title: Ivan Toney offered to Man United as January loan-to-buy move explored
item.description: Ivan Toney offered to Man United as January loan-to-buy move explored Manchester United have reportedly been offered the chance to sign Ivan Toney , as intermediaries explore a January loan with an option to buy for the Al-Ahli striker. Head coach Mauricio Pochettino inherits a side in need of attacking reinforcements Toney left Brentford for Al-Ahli on 30th August 2024 in a £40 million transfer, signing a four-year contract with the Saudi Pro League club. United’s need for reinforcements has been sharpened by Benjamin Sesko’s long-term absence. Pochettino inherited a side in 18th place with eight points from 10 Premier League matches when he replaced former head coach Michael Carrick on 13th November, and has already introduced new fitness and tactical preparation measures at Carrington. Intermediaries present Toney as a January option United are among several Premier League clubs being kept informed about Toney’s position (via TEAMtalk ). The report says: “Intermediaries are actively working behind the scenes to line up prospective options for the 30-year-old ahead of the January transfer window and beyond.” Saudi Pro League sources have indicated that formal negotiations are yet to begin, although people close to the situation believe an agreement can be reached with Al-Ahli. The proposed structure would allow Toney to return to European football before a possible permanent transfer. The outlet states: “TEAMtalk understands that a loan move featuring an option to buy is currently being explored to facilitate a transfer, with Toney keen on a return to European football.” Toney has 18 months remaining on his Al-Ahli contract and has scored 16 goals in 15 starts this season. United have been contacted directly about his availability. Pochettino is said to have strongly emphasised to the club’s hierarchy that recruiting a centre-forward must be a priority. United are assessing a shortlist of attacking targets. Toney appeals to decision-makers because they regard him as a proven Premier League focal point who would fit Pochettino’s tactical system. Reporter Graeme Bailey adds: “Crucially, we are told that a potential switch to Old Trafford is an option that would strongly appeal to Toney himself.” Arsenal, Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur have also been informed that the England international could be available. Crystal Palace manager Thomas Frank is also eager for his club to consider reuniting him with the forward he previously coached at Brentford. Toney was omitted from England’s latest squad for the Nations League matches against Croatia and Spain, but he reportedly retains ambitions of featuring in England head coach Thomas Tuchel’s plans for Euro 2028. Prospective suitors are not believed to view a court case scheduled for 2028 as a major obstacle or something affecting his career at present. item.title: NELFUND considers increase in N20,000 monthly student upkeep
item.description: By Joseph Erunke Millions of Nigerian students benefiting from the Federal Government’s student loan scheme may soon receive higher monthly upkeep allowances as the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, NELFUND, considers a review of the current N20,000 payment amid mounting pressure from rising living costs. The possibility of an increase emerged as NELFUND acknowledged that the existing allowance might require adjustment to better reflect the financial realities facing students struggling to meet the costs of feeding, transportation, accommodation and other basic necessities while pursuing their education. The fund’s Managing Director, Akintunde Sawyer, disclosed this during an interview on Beyond the Headlines,a TVC news programme, where he said the monthly upkeep payment was under constant review. Although he did not announce a new figure or a timeline for implementation, Sawyer signalled that an adjustment was being considered, raising expectations among students who have repeatedly complained that the current ₦20,000 monthly allowance is inadequate to survive on in the face of escalating prices. “Are we considering it? Yes, of course. It’s under constant review,” he said. The indication of a possible increase comes against the backdrop of growing concerns over the purchasing power of students, many of whom depend on the NELFUND intervention to cushion the financial burden of higher education. With food prices, transportation fares, accommodation costs and other essential expenses continuing to weigh heavily on households, the N20,000 monthly upkeep has increasingly come under scrutiny over its capacity to provide meaningful relief to beneficiaries. However, Sawyer said any decision to increase the allowance would have to be carefully weighed against the fund’s financial capacity and the need to sustain support for the growing number of students enrolled in the scheme. He explained that while NELFUND was conscious of the need to improve students’ welfare, it could not make adjustments without considering the implications for the entire beneficiary population. “What we need to do is plan it in such a way that it doesn’t put us in a situation where we can’t cater for the totality of the people that we need to cater for,” Sawyer said. Beyond the proposed review by NELFUND, Sawyer disclosed that President Bola Tinubu was also considering an intervention aimed at providing students with more meaningful financial support to enable them to remain in school and successfully complete their academic programmes. Although he did not disclose the nature, scope or financial details of the proposed presidential intervention, the NELFUND chief suggested that the government was exploring ways to improve the level of assistance available to students. “I know the President certainly is looking at intervening in a way that helps the students have more meaningful sustenance so that they can get through their courses,” he said. item.title: Miami’s Defense Is A Real Threat To Josh Allen’s Records
item.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports The Miami Dolphins are not a pushover just because they sit at one win and eight losses. Josh Allen knows this better than anyone. He told his teammates to watch the tape closely because the defense is doing fantastic things. The numbers back up his warning. Miami allows just 202.1 yards per game through the air, which ranks seventh in the NFL. That stat comes straight from Yahoo Sports . A team that stops the pass that well can make life miserable for any quarterback. Allen has faced Miami many times before. He owns a 14-3 career record against them. But the history lesson might not help him this time. He called the unit “very sticky” and praised the head coach for keeping the scheme in sync. According to reports, the scheme is “freakin awesome” and the players are putting in extreme effort. These are not empty words from a star player. They are a direct heads-up about the danger lurking in the opposing sideline. The Bills might be 8-1, but the Dolphins are hungry to upset. The Home Field Edge Buffalo has a massive advantage at home. They have not lost to Miami in Orchard Park since 2016. All three of Allen’s losses to the Dolphins happened in south beach. This pattern is clear from the data reported by BuffaLowDown. The Bills have won by two scores in 9 of their 14 wins since 2018. They have even scored 40 or more points in three of those matchups. The offense is ready to light up the scoreboard. But the defense has to match that energy. The Dolphins defense has been their saving grace. Ranked 10th in the NFL for total yards allowed, they average 320.6 yards per contest. Although facing difficulties in other areas, this ranking puts them within the top third of the league. NDTV Sports highlighted that the unit remains solid even when the offense stumbles. The team in Miami knows they need a perfect game to win. They cannot rely on their record to scare anyone off. Sunday Is The Test The Bills cannot treat this game as a simple formality. Allen warned that looking strictly at records misses the point. He said, “If you were looking at strictly records, one win compared to, you turn on the tape of that defense, they’re doing some fantastic things, and I’m not just saying that.” The Bills need to respect the opponent in front of them. A sloppy start could cost them the game. The matchup takes place on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 1 p.m. ET at Highmark Stadium. I think, according to reports, the Dolphins are looking to upset, but their defense gives them a shot in every game they are in. WGRZ reported that the team is focused on the challenge ahead. The Bills face a tough test that their win column does not show.

item.title: GLP-1 drugs could have a surprisingly large environmental payoff
item.description: GLP-1 weight-loss medicines such as Ozempic and Wegovy could affect much more than the waistlines of the people who take them. If widely used, our new research suggests these appetite-suppressing medicines could transform the global food system and free up vast areas of agricultural land. The global food system is ultimately driven by demand. If people eat less, producers respond, affecting production, prices, trade, and how much land is needed. We used a powerful computer simulation to explore scenarios ranging from GLP-1 use concentrated in high-income countries to widespread global access. With widespread use of these medicines among adults living with obesity, we estimate that reduced calorie intake could prevent up to 6.6 million deaths each year by 2050, while freeing up as much as 32 million hectares of agricultural land—an area slightly larger than Italy—for other uses. item.title: 30 Years Later, Sean Connery's Secret James Bond Thriller Is Officially Free on Streaming
item.description: Back in the 1990s, Michael Bay was really cooking. Before the slog that was 2001’s Pearl Harbor and his divisive Transformers movies that simultaneously hurt and enhanced his career by sidelining him for decades, Bay debuted as a director with a trio of really exciting movies that prioritized a fun experience for the viewer. First there was 1995’s Bad Boys , the Will Smith and Martin Lawrence buddy-cop film that became a popular franchise. He closed out the decade with the genre-defining end-of-the-world disaster film Armageddon . And in between those two, he gave us a tightly crafted thriller that is currently free to stream (with ads) on Pluto TV.

item.title: Nigerian sentenced to 24 months in US prison over COVID-19 relief fraud
item.description: A Nigerian man, Chukwuebuka Arinze, has been sentenced to two years in prison in the United States for using another person’s identity to fraudulently apply for COVID-19 relief funds. Arinze, 38, was convicted of aggravated identity theft after using a farmer’s Social Security number to submit an application under the US government’s Coronavirus Food Assistance Program. He was sentenced on October 30, 2026, by US District Judge Robert Rossiter Jr. at a federal court in Omaha, Nebraska, according to the US Attorney’s Office for the District of Nebraska. The Nigerian will also serve one year of supervised release after his imprisonment and face deportation from the United States, the statement said. Prosecutors said Arinze, who was living outside the US at the time, sent an email to the Farm Service Agency office in Wayne, Nebraska, on September 28, 2020, seeking financial assistance under the programme. The email, titled “CFAP Forms,” contained an application for the second phase of the Coronavirus Food Assistance Program, known as CFAP2, alongside an Automated Clearing House payment form. Both documents were submitted in the name of a dairy farmer identified in court records as Victim 1 and contained the farmer’s Social Security number. The US authorities said Arinze knowingly used the identification number belonging to the farmer without authorisation to validate the application. He was later brought to the United States to face prosecution over the offence. The Coronavirus Food Assistance Program was established by the US Department of Agriculture during the COVID-19 pandemic to support agricultural producers affected by declining sales and rising marketing costs. The initiative was administered through the department’s Farm Service Agency and Agricultural Marketing Service. Its first phase ran from May 26 to September 11, 2020, while the second phase, CFAP2, opened from September 21 to December 11 of the same year. The programme allowed applicants to self-certify their eligibility without submitting evidence of pandemic-related business losses. The Federal Bureau of Investigation investigated the case. The post Nigerian sentenced to 24 months in US prison over COVID-19 relief fraud appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ogun PDP deputy guber candidate installed Akinkanju of Egbaland
item.description: By Jimoh Babatunde The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) Deputy Governorship Candidate in Ogun State for the 2027 election, Hajia Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, has been installed as the first Akinkanju of Egbaland by the Alake and Paramount Ruler of Egbaland, Oba Adedotun Aremu Gbadebo, Okukenu IV. The installation took place at the Alake Palace on Saturday as part of activities marking the monarch’s 21st coronation anniversary. Sowunmi-Kolapo, who was previously honoured with the title of Iyalode of Ijemo, is also the Iya Sunnah of Egbaland and Ameerah of Ogun State. According to the palace, the new title, the first of its kind, was conferred on her in recognition of her contributions to the development of Egbaland and her commitment to the community. Oba Gbadebo urged her to remain committed to service, cultural preservation and the promotion of unity across Egbaland. The ceremony attracted prominent personalities, including government officials, business leaders, traditional rulers and politicians. The Ogun State PDP governorship candidate, Oladipupo Adebutu, led other party leaders to celebrate with his running mate. Speaking at the reception held at the Abeokuta Sports Club, Sowunmi-Kolapo expressed gratitude for the honour, particularly acknowledging the Alake for the recognition. She also described the conferment as significant ahead of the 2027 governorship election, saying the people of Ogun State had spoken through the honour. The deputy governorship candidate maintained that the forthcoming election should transcend party affiliations, insisting that the people must resist any alleged attempt to undermine the state’s interests. “We are indigenes of Ogun State. We do not run from battles. It is in our DNA to always resist intimidation and protect our independence. “I’m humbled by this gracious conferment of the title of the 1st Akinkanju of Egbaland on me by His Royal Majesty. “I pray to justify the confidence reposed in me by our traditional rulers, our respected elders, who have continued to stand for our heritage, the people of Egbaland, and the people of Ogun State in general. “Our father, the Alake of Egbaland, has spoken. Let us work hard to continue to have an Egba community that is first among others,” she said. Also honoured at the ceremony was Senator Iyabo Obasanjo, who was installed as the first Iyaniwura of Egbaland by the Alake. In his remarks, Adebutu congratulated his running mate and the other honourees, describing their recognition as well deserved. He said Sowunmi-Kolapo’s elevation from Iyalode of Ijemo to Akinkanju of Egbaland reflected her years of service, loyalty, courage, motherly leadership and commitment to the unity and development of the Egba people. Adebutu also congratulated Obasanjo on her installation as the first Iyaniwura of Egbaland, describing the honour as recognition of her distinguished public service and contributions to Egbaland and Nigeria. item.title: NDLEA arrests South African golfer, Kenyan chef over drug trafficking
item.description: Agency intercepts 160 explosives bound for Zamfara, seizes 4.6 tonnes of cannabis in Osun By Kingsley Omonobi The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has arrested a 37-year-old South African professional golfer, Grobler Henlo, and a 25-year-old Kenyan chef, Abubakar Faiza Njambi, over an alleged attempt to smuggle 50.40 kilogrammes of Loud, a potent strain of cannabis, into Nigeria. The suspects were arrested at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA), Ikeja, Lagos, following the interception of the illicit consignment. The NDLEA spokesman, Femi Babafemi, said the golfer’s arrest came exactly one month before the agency intercepted an American professional basketball player, Greene Da’monte Khiree, at the same airport on November 11, 2026, over the importation of 33.95 kilogrammes of the same psychoactive substance. According to the agency, Henlo arrived in Lagos from South Africa aboard a South African Airways flight on October 11 and was intercepted at the Terminal 2 arrival hall. A search of two travelling boxes in his possession reportedly led to the discovery of 46 parcels of Loud weighing 50.40 kilogrammes. Investigations revealed that although the boxes were in Henlo’s possession, they bore the luggage tags of his alleged accomplice, Njambi, who had collected two other boxes bearing his tags from the airport conveyor belt before leaving the airport. The agency said the exchange of luggage tags was a deliberate attempt by the syndicate to frustrate the identification of ownership and enable each courier to deny the boxes bearing their respective names if intercepted. During preliminary questioning, Henlo reportedly disclosed that he was recruited by a South African associate identified as Shanel, who linked him with other members of the syndicate whom he had never met physically. He said a driver picked him up from his home in South Africa, handed him four travelling boxes and took him to the airport, where he was instructed to meet Njambi and exchange luggage tags. The golfer reportedly said he was promised 5,000 South African rand upon successful delivery of the consignment. Further examination revealed that tracking devices had been installed in the travelling boxes and on his mobile phone, a development the agency said was similar to what was discovered in the bags abandoned by the American basketball player a month later. The NDLEA said the discovery showed how closely the cartels monitored their couriers and consignments. It added that the passport biodata page of Njambi, recovered from Henlo’s phone, was used to profile her and place her on the agency’s watchlist. She was subsequently arrested at the departure boarding gate of the Lagos airport on October 15 while attempting to board a South African Airways flight to Kenya. item.title: Elizabeth Agboola: Your Next Flight From Nigeria Could Be Two Holidays in One. Here’s How
item.description: Have you ever spent six hours in an airport waiting for your connecting flight, watching the departure screens, browsing duty-free shops and wondering what the city outside looks like? Perhaps you were connecting through Istanbul, Doha, Dubai or Addis Ababa. You were technically in another country, but the closest you came to experiencing it was buying a souvenir at the airport. What if I told you that some airlines could help you turn that connection into an additional holiday, sometimes even providing accommodation? Having travelled to more than 70 countries, I have learnt that one of the smartest ways to travel is to pay attention to the journey, not just the destination. Many Nigerians book international tickets based on price, travel time and baggage allowance. These are important considerations, but there is another question worth asking: What else can this ticket give me? I am talking about stopovers, not the hurried two-hour connection where you are running between terminals, but an intentional break in your journey that allows you to experience another destination before continuing to the country you originally planned to visit. And with the right airline, itinerary and travel documents, that additional experience might cost less than you imagine. First, Understand What You Are Booking A layover is generally a connection between flights; a stopover is a longer, planned break in your journey. Airlines define these differently, and the distinction matters because some offer special hotel packages, sightseeing tours or complimentary accommodation to qualifying passengers. For example, imagine travelling from Lagos to London through Istanbul. Instead of spending a few hours at Istanbul Airport, you could investigate whether your ticket qualifies for a longer stopover, allowing you to explore Istanbul before continuing to London. You have now turned one international journey into an opportunity to experience two destinations outside Nigeria. item.title: 10 things that worry me about chasing the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt
item.description: null On Aug. 2, 2027, I'll be in Luxor, Egypt, to witness what could be the greatest total solar eclipse of my life. I've seen nine total solar eclipses across the world, but this one promises to be different. For a remarkable six minutes and 22 seconds, the moon will completely cover the sun, plunging Egypt's ancient temples and monuments into eerie twilight as the solar corona bursts into view. I've been calling it the "eclipse of the century" for many years, and for good reason. It will be the longest total solar eclipse until 2114 — and the longest on land of the 21st century — and it will take place in one of the most extraordinary places on Earth. What could go wrong? I've chased eclipses long enough to know that the celestial mechanics are the easy part. The moon will arrive exactly on schedule — that's guaranteed. Everything else — the weather, the crowds, the transport, the equipment and the people — is rather less predictable. From the possibility of dust storms to uncertainty about whether boats will even be allowed to move on the Nile, there are plenty of reasons to be slightly wary about what awaits eclipse chasers after the ultimate bragging rights on Aug. 2, 2027. Here are the 10 things worrying me most about the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt. A dust storm could make the eclipsed sun less impressive. (Image credit: Grant Faint via Getty Images) 1. A sudden dust storm The chances of cloud-free skies in Luxor and anywhere in Upper Egypt in August are exceptionally high — close to 100%. That's almost unheard of in eclipse-chasing. However, clouds aren't the only thing that can obscure the sun. Dust and sand are potential hazards in the Egyptian desert, and a dust storm at the wrong moment could affect—though probably not ruin—the view. Although the sun will almost certainly be visible during the eclipse, airborne dust could hide the delicate structure of the solar corona. 2. Chaos in Luxor How many people will descend on Luxor for the eclipse? August is normally a quiet month for tourism in Luxor because of the oppressive heat. In 2027, however, the city and its surrounding urban area — population about four million — could swell as eclipse chasers, tour groups, photographers and curious visitors descend. Hotels, roads, buses and archaeological sites will all face extraordinary pressure. My biggest concern isn't necessarily the number of people watching the eclipse, but the logistical chaos it will create. Let's take Mallorca as an example for the 2026 eclipse. Authorities there had a plan for its west coast, the prime viewing region. "They were going to start closing roads from 3 p.m. on the afternoon of the eclipse," said Simon Waldram , who runs astrophotography and landscape photography workshops and who drove his tour group to the intended viewing location at 8 o'clock on the morning of the eclipse. "There were already 300 cars there, and by 11 a.m. they had shut the road." Official plans can quickly change. The banks of the

item.title: ‘I’ve not been served’ – Jimmy Odukoya speaks on court injunction amid church crisis
item.description: Pastor Jimmy Odukoya has said he has not been formally served with the court injunction restraining him from presenting himself as the Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head of The Fountain of Life Church, Ilupeju, Lagos. Odukoya made this known on Sunday while addressing the congregation during the church’s service, saying he had only heard about the injunction but had yet to receive the court order. “I heard that there was an injunction against me. I heard. I’ve not seen it. But I heard. But I’ve not been served. So, legally, I’ve not been served,” he said. His remarks came shortly after the founder of The Redeemed Evangelical Mission, Bishop Mike Okonkwo, made a surprise appearance at the service and urged members not to take sides in the leadership dispute involving Odukoya and his sister, Tolu. Thanking members for their continued support amid the controversy, Jimmy Odukoya said he appreciated their decision to attend the service despite the ongoing crisis. “In spite of everything, you are still here,” he told the congregation. He also reaffirmed his commitment to the church and its members, saying, “There is no Fountain without you. You are Fountain of Life. And as long as you are with me, I will continue to speak for you. I will continue to stand with you.” Describing the service as the quickest, Odukoya joked that Okonkwo had already delivered the sermon, leaving him with little to add. “Bishop has preached already. There is nothing to preach again,” he said, adding that he would finish speaking on time. He subsequently asked the congregation if they wanted another dance, to which members reportedly responded in the affirmative. Earlier, Okonkwo told the congregation that he was prompted by the Holy Spirit to visit the church and bless its members amid the leadership crisis. “I have not slept since 1.30 am. The Holy Spirit said to me, son, go to the Fountain and bless them. That’s why I am here,” he said. On Friday, Odukoya approached the Federal High Court in Lagos, challenging his reported removal as senior pastor and questioning the legality of decisions allegedly taken by some members of the church’s Board of Trustees. The suit, instituted alongside the Incorporated Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church, named his sister, Tolu Odukoya, and seven other church leaders as respondents. They include Pastors Rotimi Okpaise, Tobi Enuha, Gbenga Onabanjo, Fred Ohiani and Akin Osinbajo, as well as Biodun Balogun and Biodun Awosika. Odukoya is challenging the validity of meetings held by some trustees on January 22, February 28 and November 16, 2026, and the decisions allegedly reached at those meetings. He is also asking the court to determine whether the trustees could remove him as senior pastor without following the procedures stipulated in the church’s constitution. item.title: Bayelsa boat tragedy: NEMA deploys technical team as death toll rises
item.description: By Emem Idio, Yenagoa The National Emergency Management Agency ,NEMA, said it has deployed a technical team to Bayelsa State to reinforce ongoing search and rescue operations following a boat accident that has now claimed 24 lives and still counting in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area. The accident occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, at the river junction between Oweikorogha and Otuan communities. The boat was conveying passengers from Ayama to Ukubie community for a burial ceremony when it capsized. NEMA in a statement signed by Manzo Ezeki of NEMA Press Unit, said 24 survivors had been rescued, while 24 bodies had been recovered as of Saturday, bringing the number of confirmed fatalities to 24. Search and rescue operations were still ongoing at the time of the announcement. The agency disclosed that 19 of the survivors were taken to Ayama Clinic, while five others, who sustained varying degrees of injuries, were transferred to Family Care Hospital in Yenagoa for medical treatment. The deployment of the technical team followed the earlier activation of NEMA’s South-South Zonal Directorate and the mobilisation of an emergency response team from its Port Harcourt Operations Office to the accident scene. The agency said it is coordinating the rescue operation alongside the Bayelsa State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA), Nigerian Red Cross Society, Nigeria Police Force, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), local divers and other emergency responders. Governor Douye Diri visited the scene of the accident, where he expressed grief over the loss of lives and condoled with the families of the victims. He also commended the emergency agencies, security operatives, local divers and other responders for their intervention and continued efforts to locate possible survivors despite the difficult riverine terrain. NEMA expressed sympathy with the Bayelsa State Government and the families affected by the tragedy, pledging to sustain its collaboration with relevant authorities to coordinate the rescue operation. The post Bayelsa boat tragedy: NEMA deploys technical team as death toll rises appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: WAEC, NECO Exams: TRCN sets December deadline for teachers’ certification
item.description: ​​⁠‌‌​ The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN) has set December 2026 as deadline for schools to ensure that, at least, 75 per cent of their teachers are professionally certified and licensed. Dr. Ronke Soyombo, Registrar/Chief Executive of TRCN, disclosed this in an interview the Newsmen in Abuja on Sunday. She said the measure was aimed at strengthening compliance with professional teaching standards. Soyombo said schools would be required to meet the certification threshold to qualify to apply for the West African Examinations Council (WAEC) and National Examinations Council (NECO) examinations. ‘By December 2026, schools will be required to have at least 75 per cent of their teachers certified and licensed by TRCN to qualify to apply for WAEC and NECO examinations,’ she said. Soyombo said the council had integrated its website with WAEC and NECO through an Application Programming Interface (API) to enable the examination bodies verify teachers’ professional status. She said authorised officials of both examination bodies would be able to access the system using designated login credentials to determine schools’ compliance with the requirement. The registrar said TRCN had commenced compliance monitoring, adding that it was engaging private school owners and administrators to encourage teachers to register for professional examinations and licensing. She, however, expressed concern over the low level of compliance, noting that many teachers had passed the professional qualifying examination but failed to complete the licensing process. ‘Our position is that every practising teacher must be professionally licensed. “Teaching without the required professional credentials would no longer be tolerated,” she said Soyombo said the council was also implementing an Accelerated Teacher Professionalisation Pathway to enable teachers without professional teaching qualifications to acquire the necessary training. She disclosed that during a recent teacher recruitment exercise in Nasarawa, TRCN personnel discovered that 250 applicants had presented fake certificates out of approximately 1,000 applicants. She advised school owners to verify certificates presented by prospective employees, explaining that TRCN certificates carried QR codes that could be scanned to confirm their authenticity. The registrar added that the council was taking action against impersonation and certificate fraud, disclosing that a suspect identified as Godfrey had been remanded in prison. On improving service delivery, Soyombo said TRCN had established a six-member call centre to receive and address teachers’ complaints relating to registration, examinations and certification around the clock. She said the council had also decentralised its operations into geographical regions, with designated personnel responsible for attending to complaints and ensuring quicker responses. item.title: School building collapses, kills pupil in Abia
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA -Tragedy struck at Ehere Community Primary School, in Obingwa LGA, Abia State, last Friday, when a pupil, identified as Vincent Chiedozie Dum, was reportedly killed by a collapsed building at the school. Nine other pupils escaped death as they fled before the collapse of the building. The deceased, a primary two pupil,was said to have gone to ease himself beside the dilapidated building when the wall suddenly collapsed on him. Principal of Ehere Community Senior Secondary School, Mr. Nwogu Chioma Allen, said they have been warning the pupils and students about the dangers of going around the dilapidated buildings in the compound. Nwogu stated the deceased pupil was rescued and taken to three hospitals who rejected for medical attention. However, he said the boy was later admitted at the Abia State University Teaching Hospital, ABSUTH, Aba. He also disclosed that about 10 pupils and students were playing around the building when it suddenly collapsed and hit the victim while the pupils escaped. The Principal said; “This place contains five institutions; the Ministry of Education, Primary Schools 1 and 2 and Ehere Community Junior and Senior Secondary Schools. We have a building here that is very weak. The building over the years, has lost its strength. You know children, they have been running around and we have been chasing them , telling them not to go around the building. “Unfortunately, that afternoon, they were running around the place, up to 10 of them went , running around that building. My teachers were shouting to them, leave that area. Incidentally, the building fell on the boy, the other children were able to escape. The boy was taken to three hospitals for medical attention, but they all rejected him.” He urged the state government to extend it’s school rehabilitation projects to the Ehere Community Primary and Secondary School. “Some of the buildings here are weak. The government has been trying in the renovation of schools. We hope that our own school will be renovated to avert such situations.” When Vanguard visited the school, it was observed that the dilapidated building has been sealed off. The post School building collapses, kills pupil in Abia appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: First-Class degree not enough to make excellent teacher – TRCN
item.description: The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN) says possessing a first-class degree does not automatically make an individual an excellent teacher. Dr. Ronke Soyombo, Registrar/Chief Executive of TRCN, stated this in an interview with Newsmen on Sunday in Abuja. Soyombo stressed the importance of professional competence adding that effective teaching required more than academic qualifications. The registrar explained that teachers must demonstrate competence in five critical areas assessed through the Council’s professional qualifying examination. She identified the areas as basic mathematics, foundational literacy, digital literacy, pedagogy, and safeguarding and child protection. According to her, teachers must possess a sound understanding of basic mathematical concepts to effectively support children’s learning and development. She described foundational literacy as equally important, noting that strong literacy skills enabled teachers to support learning across other subject areas. The registrar said teachers must also understand today’s children, particularly those belonging to the Alpha Generation, and the technological environment in which they operate. She identified digital literacy as the third major area of assessment, describing it as compulsory for teachers seeking to engage effectively with contemporary learners. To illustrate the challenge, Soyombo recalled visiting an examination centre where she encountered an elderly teacher struggling with a computer mouse. “I remember visiting an examination centre recently and meeting an elderly teacher who held a computer mouse and asked me, ‘Madam, what am I going to do with this?’” she said. She said the encounter highlighted the extent of digital literacy challenges confronting some teachers and raised concerns about their preparedness for modern classrooms. “How can teachers effectively engage children in today’s classrooms if they are not comfortable with basic technology?” she asked. Soyombo, however, acknowledged the challenges and disclosed that several training programmes were being implemented to improve teachers’ digital competence. On pedagogy, she said possessing excellent academic qualifications did not automatically translate into the ability to teach effectively. “Having a first-class degree does not automatically make someone an excellent teacher,” she said. She explained that academic qualifications alone could not guarantee that a teacher understood how to apply appropriate instructional methods to address different learning needs. According to her, classrooms comprise learners with varying abilities, including average pupils, children requiring additional support, and gifted and talented learners. She stressed that teachers must possess the pedagogical skills to effectively reach all categories of learners and ensure inclusive classroom experiences. “This is why pedagogy is a critical component of our examination. “Without sound pedagogical skills, a person cannot b

item.title: Full list: FG announces 19 international job vacancies [How to apply]
item.description: The Federal Government, FG has announced 19 international job vacancies for qualified Nigerians at the African Space Agency and the General Secretariat of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC). The vacancies, announced by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, comprise five positions at the African Space Agency headquarters in Cairo, Egypt, and 14 positions at the OIC headquarters in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. The ministry disclosed this in two separate vacancy announcements dated Friday, November 20, 2026, signed by its spokesperson, Oluwafemi Adeniyi, and shared on its official Facebook page on Saturday. According to the ministry, the African Space Agency is recruiting for five positions, with application deadlines of November 25 and December 10, 2026. The positions include Director, Corporate Services (D-1); Director-General, African Space Agency (D-2); Head of Legal Affairs (Grade P-5); Senior Finance Officer (P3); and Senior Human Resources Officer (P3). The ministry said interested and qualified Nigerians should visit the agency’s official website at https://africanspaceagency.org for details of the eligibility requirements and application procedures. For the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, the ministry announced 14 vacancies across its departments and specialised units. The positions include Director-General of Political Affairs; Director, Administration Department; Director, Information Department; Director, Conference Department; Director, Muslim Communities and Minorities; Director, African Affairs; and Director, European Affairs and International Organisations. Others are Head of Human Resources (PP2); Professional Officer, Human Resources (PP2); Professional Officers, Administration Department (P2); Director, Peace, Security and Mediation Unit; Chief of HRC Office – IUT; Registrar – IUT; and Deputy Internal Auditor – IUT. item.title: Dickson mourns victims of Bayelsa boat mishap, seeks safety measures
item.description: Former Governor of Bayelsa State, Senator Henry Seriake Dickson, has commiserated with the families and friends of victims of the boat mishap along the Ayama/Oweikorogha waterways in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of the state. Dickson, who disclosed this in a post on his X platform on Sunday, described the incident as unfortunate and expressed sadness over the loss of lives. He also extended his condolences to the Bayelsa State Government and the people of the state over the tragedy. The senator said he deliberately scaled down his engagements on Saturday as a mark of respect for those who lost their lives in the incident. According to him, he reduced the number of visitors he attended to and cancelled some previously scheduled visits to reflect on the tragedy. Dickson commended the relevant emergency response agencies and other individuals involved in the rescue operation for their swift response, urging them to sustain their efforts until the operation was successfully concluded. He also called for stricter enforcement of maritime safety regulations and increased public awareness to prevent similar incidents. The former governor stressed the need for continuous safety education for marine operators, security personnel and residents of Bayelsa State. He further urged traditional institutions and the media to support efforts aimed at promoting maritime safety and ensuring compliance with relevant regulations. Dickson reiterated his condolences to the bereaved families, praying that God would grant the deceased eternal rest and give their loved ones the strength to bear the loss. item.title: APOD: 2026 November 22 – Swirls and Colors on Jupiter from Juno
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 22 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Swirls and Colors on Jupiter from Juno Explanation: What creates the colors in Jupiter’s clouds? No one is sure. The thick atmosphere of Jupiter is mostly hydrogen and helium , elements which are colorless at the low temperatures of the Jovian cloud tops . Which trace molecules provide the colors remains a topic of research , although small amounts of ammonium hydrosulfide are one leading candidate . What is clear from the featured color-enhanced image — and many similar images — is that lighter clouds are typically higher up than darker ones. Pictured, light clouds swirl around reddish regions toward the lower right, while they appear to cover over some darker domains on the upper right. The featured image was taken by the robotic Juno spacecraft in 2018 during its 14th low pass over Jupiter . Juno continues in its looping elliptical orbit, swooping near the huge planet every 33 days and exploring a slightly different sector each time around. item.title: Review: Godzilla Minus Zero joins the list of truly stellar sequels
item.description: It's a rare thing for a film sequel to match or even surpass its predecessor; The Godfather Part II and Terminator 2: Judgement Day are the best known examples on a pretty short list. Go ahead and add Godzilla Minus Zero to that list. Director Takashi Yamazaki's sequel to his critically acclaimed Godzilla Minus One (2023) is everything one could want in a Godzilla movie: human pathos, great special effects, and, ultimately, two giant kaiju duking it out over who gets to destroy Japan (and eventually the world) the most. (Spoilers for the first film below. Spoilers for Minus Zero but no major reveals until after the gallery. We'll give you a heads-up when we get there.) As I wrote previously , Yamazaki wanted to return to Godzilla’s filmic roots with Minus One , setting the events in postwar Japan and tapping into the monster’s symbolic representation of the Japanese perspective on the 1940s nuclear holocaust—while also incorporating all-too-human themes of guilt and redemption. That first film focused on kamikaze pilot Kōichi Shikishima (Ryunosuke Kamiki), who struggled with survivor’s guilt after he failed to take action when Godzilla attacked the Japanese base on Odo Island in 1945. item.title: ‘I Struggled To Come Out, Lost My Sister, Other Relatives,’ Bayelsa Boat Accident Survivor
item.description: A survivor of Friday’s boat accident in the Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has recounted how she struggled to escape from the capsized vessel, saying she lost several members of her family and neighbours in the tragedy. The woman, whose identity was not immediately disclosed, said her elder sister, her sister’s daughter-in-law and two children belonging to her relatives and neighbours were among those who died in the accident. Recounting the incident, she said the boat suddenly capsized, trapping passengers beneath it. “The boat just fell and pressed all of us. My elder sister’s son’s wife was lost. My elder sister was lost. Her son was also lost. One of my neighbours who followed us also lost her son. My neighbour herself was lost,” she said. ﻿ The survivor said she was the only person among those close to her who made it out alive, adding that she struggled to escape after the boat overturned. “It’s only me that is safe. When I came out, somebody held me. I was drinking water. I was not able to come out. I struggled before I came out. Where we were standing, the boat broke from above and pressed us down,” she said. Asked by the Bayelsa governor, Douye Diri, whether the bodies of her missing relatives and neighbours had been recovered, she replied in the negative. Her account comes as the death toll from the accident has risen to 23, while 24 survivors are receiving treatment in hospitals. The accident occurred near Oweikorogha Community in the Ukubie area of Southern Ijaw when a boat conveying mourners from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony capsized at about 11 a.m. on Friday. ﻿ The Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed the incident, saying preliminary findings indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways. However, a survivor had also alleged that the wooden passenger vessel, popularly known as a ‘love boat’, was overloaded with passengers and their belongings, raising concerns about possible breaches of waterway safety regulations. President Bola Tinubu has expressed condolences to the families of the victims and directed relevant federal disaster response agencies to support rescue and recovery operations. In a statement posted on his X account, Tinubu described the incident as tragic and said those who died did not deserve to lose their lives in such circumstances. “Those who lost their lives in the tragedy did not deserve to die that way. I have directed all relevant Federal Disaster Response agencies to work together to ensure a successful recovery and rescue operation,” he said. The President also directed that Saturday’s presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, be held without much fanfare in honour of the victims. Meanwhile, Governor Diri has visited the scene of the accident and is expected to initiate an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the tragedy. item.title: Can Enzo Maresca Win The Premier League In His First Season At Man City?
item.description: Six league titles. Ten years. A stand at the Etihad with his name on it. Good luck following that. Enzo Maresca has to, after Manchester City unveiled him as manager back in June 2026. Maresca at least knows his way around the training ground. Back in 2020-2021, he ran the Elite Development Squad and won Premier League 2 with them. He returned in 2022 to work under Guardiola as an assistant, and that season ended with the treble. So this is spell number three, and he’s tied down until 2029. Expectations at City don’t reset just because the man in the dugout has changed. City’s title odds have become some of the most debated in premier league online betting markets because bookmakers must weigh a campaign shaped as much by events off the pitch as on it. A Flying Start, Then A Bump The opening weeks went better than almost anyone expected. Maresca became the first manager in Premier League history to win his first seven games in charge of a new club. The football looked familiar too. City kept the ball and wore teams down, which is no surprise from a coach who learned so much from Guardiola. His Leicester and Chelsea sides played the same way. City spent big to help him. Their summer outlay of around £460 million was a record for any club, and £125 million of it went on Enzo Fernández from Chelsea, a fee that matched the Premier League transfer record. Phil Foden signed a four-year extension. Rodri, one of the faces of the Guardiola years, left for Barcelona. Maresca has won quickly before. He lifted the Championship title with Leicester in 2023-24. A year later at Chelsea, he won the Conference League and the Club World Cup and still finished fourth in the league. Seven straight wins at the start of a season guarantee nothing, of course. Plenty of fast starters have slid down the Premier League table once the winter fixtures arrive. City soon lost three league games in a row, one of them a 1-0 home defeat to Brighton, who had never won away at City before. Then there are Arsenal. Mikel Arteta, another former Guardiola assistant, ended their 22-year wait for the title in 2025-26, helped along by a Premier League record for goals from corners. Manchester City’s Italian manager Enzo Maresca gestures on the touchline during the English Premier League football match between Manchester City and Sunderland at the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, north west England, on September 20, 2026. (Photo by PETER POWELL / AFP) The Fight Off the Pitch The bigger problem might be off the pitch entirely. Early in the 2026-27 season, an independent commission found City guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules. It ruled that the club used “sham” contracts with commercial partners to inflate revenues and cut costs by more than £900 million between 2009 and 2018. City deny any wrongdoing and have appealed. If the verdict stands, they face a heavy sanction, and a big points deduction is one of the options on the table. So Maresca could get everythi

item.title: Death Toll In Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 23
item.description: The death toll from Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 23, with 24 survivors receiving treatment in hospitals. The accident occurred when a boat conveying mourners to a burial ceremony capsized near Oweikorogha Community in the Ukubie area of Southern Ijaw. The Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed the incident in a statement, saying the boat was travelling from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony on Friday, when it capsized at about 11 a.m. A preliminary police report indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways. Following the incident, rescue operations were launched, with several passengers rescued while others were initially reported missing. A survivor had also alleged that the wooden passenger boat, popularly known as a ‘love boat’, was overloaded with passengers and their belongings, suggesting that this might have contributed to the accident. President Bola Tinubu has expressed condolences to the families of the victims, describing the incident as tragic and directing relevant federal disaster response agencies to support rescue and recovery efforts. In a statement posted on his X account, Tinubu said, “Those who lost their lives in the tragedy did not deserve to die that way. I have directed all relevant Federal Disaster Response agencies to work together to ensure a successful recovery and rescue operation.” The President also directed that the presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, on Saturday, be held without much fanfare in honour of those who lost their lives. “On behalf of the entire nation, I mourn those who lost their lives in the incident and sympathise with their families, the government and the people of Bayelsa State. “I particularly mourn with Governor Douye Diri over this sad incident. I pray that God Almighty repose their souls and comfort their families,” he said. Meanwhile, Governor Douye Diri has visited the scene of the accident and is expected to initiate a probe into the circumstances surrounding the tragedy. item.title: China Diaries: The Railway Connecting Continents
item.description: Standing at the Xi’an International Port Station in northwest China, watching the movement of freight trains preparing to transport goods across borders and continents, I was reminded that economic development is not only about what a country produces. It is also about how efficiently it can move what it produces to the rest of the world. Xi’an occupies an interesting place in China’s history. It was once the starting point of the ancient Silk Road, which connected China to Central Asia, the Middle East and Europe through centuries of trade and cultural exchange. Today, the city is reclaiming that historic role through a modern railway network that connects Chinese manufacturing centres to markets across Europe and Asia. The China-Europe Railway Express is one of the most visible outcomes of China’s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). Through this network, freight trains transport automobiles, electronics, machinery, textiles, agricultural products and other goods across the Eurasian continent. What makes the initiative particularly interesting is how it has transformed the economic possibilities of a city located thousands of kilometres from the sea. Xi’an has become an important international logistics hub, demonstrating that geographical distance from a coastline does not have to limit a city’s participation in global trade. The railway network has continued to expand. By November 2025, China-Europe freight trains had completed nearly 120,000 journeys, connecting 232 cities in 26 European countries and more than 100 cities in 11 Asian countries. The value of goods transported through the network had reached $426.4 billion by the end of 2024. These are not merely impressive transportation figures. They represent an evolving system of economic connectivity, linking manufacturers, suppliers, distributors and consumers across national borders. Beyond transportation: The economics of connectivity The significance of the railway goes beyond moving containers from one destination to another. It creates opportunities for businesses to reach markets faster, diversify their supply chains and reduce their dependence on a single transportation route. Rail freight offers an important middle ground between air and sea transportation. While it is generally more expensive than shipping by sea, it can be considerably faster. For certain categories of goods, particularly machinery, automobile components, electronics and other time-sensitive products, that difference can be commercially significant. It also provides an alternative when disruptions affect other transportation routes. Another important feature is the development of inland logistics infrastructure. Warehousing, customs processing, container handling, industrial parks and distribution services have grown around railway connections. This means the economic benefits are not confined to the railway operators. They extend to businesses, workers and communities along the routes. This is an important lesson i

item.title: Drone attack sets Russian cargo ship ablaze in Gulf of Finland
item.description: A Russian cargo ship caught fire after ​being hit by drones in the Baltic Sea on Saturday and drifted into Finnish waters. Reporting from Kyiv, FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg notes that the ship is affiliated with a major Russian military logistics company. While Ukrainian authorities typically neither confirm nor deny responsibility, analysts cite a clear motive for the targeting, Cragg explains.

item.title: The FBI and USDA were reportedly hacked
item.description: Friday, it was reported that both the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) and the FBI were hacked. In reporting on the FBI hack, CNN noted that this is the second such attack on the agency in the last few months, this time targeting the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), which federal, state, and local law enforcement use to share information, including warrants and missing persons. President Donald Trump later confirmed the hack in an interview with Fox News . NBC first reported the USDA hack on Friday. According to Reuters : While the payments ​database is the known extent ​of the intrusion so far, the former ‌officials ⁠warned that … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: COP31: Deep divisions persist over energy, finance and science
item.description: COP31 climate talks in Turkey have gone into overtime, with deep divisions over fossil fuels, climate finance and global warming targets delaying an agreement. A revised draft dropped all mention of fossil fuels, prompting strong criticism from the EU and a dozen countries demanding a clear commitment to phase them out. Negotiators are also split over a proposed global electrification target, carbon capture and the future of UN climate science reports. Developing nations have voiced anger over the removal of a $120 billion climate adaptation funding target. Australia is now racing to secure a revised deal before delegates leave. France 24 journalist Adria Rocha Cutiller tells us the latest.

item.title: FBI criminal database hacked
item.description: The FBI is investigating a reported major cyberattack targeting its national law enforcement database, the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), which holds sensitive criminal justice records, including information on fugitives, missing persons, criminal histories and stolen property. President Donald Trump said he had just been briefed on the incident, describing it as “not good”. FRANCE 24’s Fraser Jackson reports from Washington DC.

item.title: Man convicted of starting palisades fire
item.description: A Los Angeles County jury found former rideshare driver Jonathan Rinderknecht guilty on Friday of starting the 2025 Palisades fire, which caused widespread destruction and loss of life. He faces a prison sentence of between five and 40 years. Liza Kaminov has more.

item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
item.description: null On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible. Danish astronomer Ole Rømer (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons) Why it mattered Understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics. "The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."

item.title: Endurance athlete swims in Hormuz Strait
item.description: The Strait of Hormuz remains largely blocked, with Iran attacking vessels attempting to cross it. As concerns grow over the environmental impact of the war, with toxic chemicals spreading through the air and sea, one swimmer and ocean advocate has gone a step further than issuing warnings: he plunged into the polluted and dangerous waters of the strait, calling on all sides to end the conflict.

item.title: France: Demonstrations losing steam as movement enters sixth week
item.description: Around 2,200 people took part in protests across France by 2pm local time, according to the Interior Ministry, which recorded 44 demonstrations nationwide and seven arrests, with the situation described as generally calm. Turnout was lower than on previous Saturdays. Reporting from Place de la République in Paris, FRANCE 24’s Antonia Kerrigan said rent rights organisations had also joined the sixth consecutive Saturday of protests, highlighting their growing pan-European dimension, with demonstrations taking place in seven European countries, including Spain, Portugal, Greece and Germany, where rising living costs and access to affordable housing are among the main concerns.

item.title: Amazon’s first digital photo frame is up to 50 percent off for Black Friday
item.description: Amazon only announced its first digital photo frame less than a month ago, but it’s already getting a sizable discount for Black Friday. You can currently grab the Alexa Photo Frame at Amazon and Best Buy starting at $114 ($115 off), making it a great holiday gift for anyone who loves displaying family photos. If you prefer the walnut trim over the birch or standard black models, it’s also on sale at Best Buy for $134.99 ($95 off) — which, like with the others, is the first discount we’ve seen. Amazon Alexa Photo Frame Where to Buy: $229.99 $114.99 at Amazon (birch) $199.99 $114.99 at Best Buy (black) $229.99 $134.99 at Best Buy (walnut) The Alexa Photo Frame features a 10-inch, semi-matte touchscreen that’s designed to make digital photos look more natural, with built-in light sensors that automatically adjust brightness throughout the day. It displays images from Amazon Photos, which supports uploads from both iOS and Android devices, including photos stored in iCloud. You can choose which people or albums to display, or let Alexa Plus do the work, which often results in photos based on your facial expression, the season, and even the lighting. You can also search for specific photos with voice commands, letting you easily pull up images of your first dog, your child as a baby, and other shots without having to scroll endlessly through years of photos yourself. If you want to add a more personal touch, Amazon also lets you attach voice notes to individual photos via the Amazon Photos app. For example, you can add a recording of your kid explaining their Halloween costume to a trick-or-treating photo. Plus, you can preload the frame with photos and recordings before gifting it, so your loved one won’t have to spend time setting it up. We’re still testing Amazon’s answer to the Aura frame, but it looks like a particularly good option if you’re already an Amazon Prime member. A Prime subscription grants you unlimited full-resolution photo storage and access to Alexa Plus at no additional cost, and unlike Amazon’s smart displays, the frame doesn’t serve up annoying ads. That said, you don’t need a subscription to use it, and new users can always access a limited-time trial of Alexa Plus.

item.title: Can Anthropic afford to put safety first?
item.description: Today, I’m talking with Hayden Field, The Verge ’s senior AI reporter, about the Anthropic IPO for the third and final episode in our series about AI in real life. The AI lab behind Claude went public on the Nasdaq last Thursday. The numbers are gigantic, but not really that important for this conversation, except to say that Anthropic has become one of the most valuable companies on the planet. The real story is what happens now — and whether Anthropic can continue to thread the needle of caring about and investing in AI safety while also being a public company beholden to shareholders. Oh, and it also continuously growing the amount of money it makes so it can keep paying its ever-increasing compute bills, which total roughly $900 billion over the coming years. All of these ideas sit in a fascinating tension with one another, and so Hayden and I really tried to break down how we think this might play out as Anthropic navigates the pressures of the public markets. You’ll hear us talk about the company’s unique corporate governance structure , something that is especially relevant in the wake of the ongoing Jensen Huang saga. We also get into why OpenAI seems happy to have let Anthropic go public first , and why Anthropic’s whole pitch to big customers boils down to the same safety branding that now sits in conflict with the profit-oriented part of its business. Before we get going, do me a favor and subscribe to Decoder on YouTube, where we put out new episodes every Monday and Thursday. Okay: Hayden Field, The Verge ’s senior AI reporter, on the Anthropic IPO and the economics of frontier AI. Here we go. This interview has been lightly edited for length and clarity. Hayden Field, welcome back to Decoder . Thanks. Great to be here. I’m excited to talk to you today because it’s not pure soap opera drama chaos. I know. It’s like a normal thing that happened. It’s for once not personality-based and soap opera. It’s about cold, hard would-be cash. [Laughs] Well, there is some personality in it because we’re going to talk a lot about Anthropic’s IPO, which has a bunch of big personalities in it, and the way they have structured this company to repel the rapacious pressures of capitalism is, I would say, very eccentric. It reflects the beliefs of a number of eccentric people. Yep, absolutely. It’s really been interesting digging into the S-1 again and just seeing who was on what committee and which founders have the most control here and how much control the founders actually have, which is more than it may seem. Let’s start at the start. You and I are talking on IPO day. Anthropic is the first pure AI lab to go public. They priced the IPO at $83 a share and they got all the way up to $111. By the time people are listening to this, who knows what the price will actually be, but it’s been a real victory lap for all the people who are invested in Anthropic. item.title: 'Star Trek: First Contact' at 30: Resistance is futile when it comes to the 'Next Generation' crew's greatest big-screen adventure
item.description:
Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

Following the sad news of Sir Patrick Stewart's passing , there's been no shortage of discussion about his best moments as Captain Jean-Luc Picard . "The Inner Light"'s life in 25 minutes is a strong contender, as are the courtroom grandstanding in "The Measure of a Man" and his insistence (under extreme torture) that "there are four lights!" in "Chain of Command". But for this writer's money, it's hard to look past a nine-minute sequence in "Star Trek: First Contact", which turns 30 this weekend. With the Borg overrunning the newly launched USS Enterprise-E, Picard — who has long-standing beef with the Collective, following his assimilation in classic "The Next Generation" story " The Best of Both Worlds " — orders his crew to fight the cybernetic nasties hand-to-hand if required, defying their pleas to activate the ship's self-destruct system and retreat. He even calls Worf — not a man renowned for dodging a fight — a coward, prompting the Klingon to respond that, "If you were any other man, I would kill you where you stand." Ouch. But following some impassioned talk about making the Borg "pay for what they've done", he's finally talked down from his rage by 21st-century stowaway Lily Sloane (Alfre Woodard). She points out that his Moby-Dick-esque obsession is on the verge of going full Ahab, and he eventually sees sense, issuing the order to abandon the Enterprise and destroy the hive. It's a masterclass showcasing the ever-brilliant Stewart's impressive range, as the out-of-control captain's rarely seen temper reaches fever pitch, before normal service is resumed. His subsequent apology to Worf — "As a matter of fact, I think you're the bravest man I've ever known" — is simply perfect. And just as the franchise's zenith, "The Wrath of Khan", is built around Kirk and Khan's decades-old feud, "First Contact" is precision engineered to get the most out of Jean-Luc. This was the right "Star Trek" at the right time, a film that put "TNG"'s greatest villains on a collision course with the origins of Starfleet. It's not quite "Khan", of course — what is? — but it deserves to be mentioned in the same breath. (Image credit: Paramount) In 1996, the "odd numbers bad, even num

item.title: Our go-to earbuds for taking calls have fallen to their lowest price to date
item.description: The Liberty 5 Pro are Soundcore’s most ambitious earbuds to date. | Photo: John Higgins / The Verge If you’re looking for a new pair of earbuds, the Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro are on sale for $129.99 at Amazon , Best Buy , and Walmart right now. That’s the lowest price we’ve seen for Anker’s excellent wireless earbuds, which normally retail for $169.99 and come in four colors (black, white, blue, and pink) all of which are discounted through November 30th as part of Anker’s ongoing Black Friday promo . Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro Where to Buy: $169.99 $129.99 at Amazon $169.99 $129.99 at Walmart $169.99 $129.99 at Best Buy While the Liberty 5 Pro have a number of great features — including support LDAC for high-res audio and an IP55 dust and water resistance rating — the call quality is what stands out. The microphone does an impressive job cutting out background noise, and my colleague John Higgins praised the Liberty 5 Pro for filtering out emergency vehicles, arborists cutting tree branches, and even loud children. The active noise cancellation is excellent, which helps when you’re trying to hear someone on the other end of the phone whose earbuds aren’t as clear as yours. The charging case also features a handy 0.96-inch screen, so you can adjust the ANC and sound profile on the fly. Read our Anker Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro review .
